AI.result: For identical initial conditions, r_k* increases monotonically with arrival rank and converges, as population size grows, to a large-N quantile limit where a finite optimum exists only above a critical rank fraction φ_c ≈ 0.412. Spatial heterogeneity qualitatively reorganizes the sequence, shifting the optimum's maximum from late to early ranks even without particle interactions. In the compared systems, sensitivity to resetting rises strongly with arrival rank, and deviations from non-interacting baselines expose effects of direct interactions, finite return overhead, and environmental memory.
AI.conclusion: Optimal resetting in multiparticle search is governed by the required completion rank and must be assessed relative to protocol- and geometry-matched baselines; naive non-interacting or first-arrival references can misestimate the optimal strategy.

title: Correlation-assisted spin-selective metallicity in strained and bilayer altermagnets
summary: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with a momentum-dependent spin-split electronic structure, providing a route to spin-polarized carriers without ferromagnetism. Here, we investigate how electronic correlations, doping, uniaxial strain, and interlayer coupling control altermagnetism within a minimal Hubbard-type model for mono- and bilayer systems. Comparing Hartree--Fock theory with the rotationally invariant slave-boson (RISB) approach, we demonstrate the robustness of altermagnetic order against quasiparticle renormalization and reveal a separation between the onset of magnetic order and the loss of quasiparticle coherence at stronger coupling. In the monolayer, doping produces a pronounced particle--hole asymmetry, while its combination with uniaxial strain generates a fully spin-polarized Fermi surface close to half-filling. In the bilayer, stacking that favors ferroic alignment of the layer altermagnetic order parameters allows their momentum-dependent spin splittings to combine constructively. Weak asymmetric doping additionally induces intra-unit-cell charge order, resulting in fully spin-polarized low-energy carriers. At a bilayer filling of five electrons in four orbitals, we find a continuous paramagnet-to-altermagnet transition followed, at stronger coupling, by an evolution toward a Mott-like regime with strongly suppressed quasiparticle weight. Our results establish correlations, strain, doping, and stacking as complementary means of controlling altermagnetic metals and generating fully spin-polarized Fermi surfaces.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how electron correlations, doping, uniaxial strain, and interlayer coupling control altermagnetism in a minimal Hubbard-type model for mono- and bilayer systems, finding robust altermagnetic order and routes to fully spin-polarized Fermi surfaces.
AI.motivation: Altermagnets offer spin-polarized carriers without net magnetization, making them attractive for spintronics, but a systematic understanding of how electronic correlations, doping, strain, and interlayer coupling govern altermagnetism is lacking.
AI.method: The authors use a minimal Hubbard-type model for monolayer and bilayer systems, comparing Hartree–Fock theory with the rotationally invariant slave-boson (RISB) approach to capture correlation effects.
AI.result: Altermagnetic order is robust against quasiparticle renormalization, with a separation between magnetic ordering onset and loss of quasiparticle coherence. Doping produces pronounced particle–hole asymmetry in the monolayer, and with uniaxial strain yields a fully spin-polarized Fermi surface near half-filling. In the bilayer, ferroically aligned layer order parameters combine constructively; weak asymmetric doping induces intra-unit-cell charge order and fully spin-polarized carriers. At five electrons in four orbitals, a continuous paramagnet-to-altermagnet transition evolves toward a Mott-like regime.
AI.conclusion: Correlations, strain, doping, and stacking act as complementary control knobs for altermagnetic metals and for generating fully spin-polarized Fermi surfaces.

title: A low-symmetry ground state of dense two-dimensional hydrogen
summary: Hydrogen under pressure is an extremely complex system featuring molecular dissociation, metallization, and anomalous melting. While bulk hydrogen has been studied for nearly a century, its two-dimensional counterpart remains unexplored. Using first-principles structural searches and relaxations in supercells containing up to 512 atoms, we identify ground-state structures of dense two-dimensional hydrogen showing no evidence of long-range crystalline order over the simulated length scales. Within density functional theory, these structures have lower enthalpy than all crystalline candidates considered over an intermediate pressure interval between molecular and atomic crystals. This preference already emerges with classical nuclei and persists as the supercell size increases, while the dominant structure-factor peaks grow substantially more slowly than in the crystalline reference phases. Although crystals with very large primitive cells cannot be rigorously excluded, these findings support the possibility of a disordered ground state and identify dense two-dimensional hydrogen as a promising setting for investigating competition between crystallization and structural disorder.

AI.tldr: Dense two-dimensional hydrogen is predicted to favor a disordered ground state over an intermediate pressure range, bridging molecular and atomic crystals.
AI.motivation: Bulk hydrogen under pressure has been studied intensively, but its two-dimensional counterpart remains unexplored, leaving open the question of how reduced dimensionality affects the competition between crystallization and disorder.
AI.method: First-principles structural searches and relaxations in supercells containing up to 512 atoms, comparing enthalpy of candidate structures within density functional theory and analyzing structure-factor peak growth with supercell size.
AI.result: Ground-state structures of dense two-dimensional hydrogen show no evidence of long-range crystalline order over the simulated length scales and have lower enthalpy than all considered crystalline candidates over an intermediate pressure interval between molecular and atomic crystals. This preference emerges already with classical nuclei and persists as supercell size increases, while dominant structure-factor peaks grow substantially more slowly than in crystalline reference phases.
AI.conclusion: Although crystals with very large primitive cells cannot be rigorously excluded, the findings support a possible disordered ground state and identify dense two-dimensional hydrogen as a promising setting for investigating the competition between crystallization and structural disorder.

title: Quantitative Classical Relaxation Dynamics of Penning-Ionized He/Ne--H$_2^+$/HD$^+$ Complexes
summary: Penning ionization allows {\it in situ} generation of ionic complexes to launch vibrational relaxation and dissociation dynamics for rare gas--H$_2^+$/HD$^+$ complexes. The ensuing translational kinetic energy release (TKER) spectra characterizing the diatomic cation are a particularly sensitive way to probe the long range part of the intermolecular interactions. TKER distributions from quasi-classical trajectory (QCT) simulations for the Ne--H$_2^+$ and Ne--HD$^+$ complexes quantitatively match measured positions and relative intensities of most experimentally observed features and are also on par with time-dependent quantum simulations. Specifically, the QCT-simulations allow to separate signatures arising from H$_2^+$/HD$^+$ relaxation into different final vibrational states, such as for $(v=2) \rightarrow (v' = 0/1 )$. Trajectory-resolved QCT analysis also provides mechanistic interpretations of the spatial and time-dependent dynamics underlying the TKER distributions. Rare gas--H$_2^+$/HD$^+$ complex lifetimes directly correlate with the final rotational quantum number $j'$ of the diatomic. Low-$j'$ products are associated primarily with an initial axial approach of the rare gas atom, whereas formation of higher-$j'$ states predominantly results from an initial T-shaped approach geometry.

AI.tldr: Quasi-classical trajectory simulations of Ne--H$_2^+$/HD$^+$ complexes reproduce experimental TKER spectra, match quantum results, and reveal that complex lifetimes and product rotational states depend on the initial approach geometry (axial vs. T-shaped).
AI.motivation: Penning ionization enables in situ formation of ionic rare gas--H$_2^+$/HD$^+$ complexes, and the resulting TKER spectra offer a sensitive probe of the long-range intermolecular interaction. A mechanistic and quantitative understanding of the vibrational relaxation and dissociation dynamics, including how initial approach geometry maps onto final rotational states and complex lifetimes, is needed.
AI.method: Quasi-classical trajectory (QCT) simulations of Penning-ionization-generated Ne--H$_2^+$ and Ne--HD$^+$ complexes, compared against experimental TKER distributions and time-dependent quantum simulations. Trajectory-resolved analysis separates contributions from different final vibrational states and correlates initial approach geometry with final rotational quantum number $j'$.
AI.result: QCT TKER distributions quantitatively match the positions and relative intensities of most experimentally observed features and are on par with quantum simulations. The simulations resolve vibrational relaxation channels such as $(v=2)\rightarrow(v'=0/1)$. Complex lifetimes correlate directly with the final rotational quantum number $j'$: low-$j'$ products arise mainly from initial axial approach, while higher-$j'$ states predominantly originate from an initial T-shaped geometry.
AI.conclusion: QCT simulations provide a quantitatively accurate and mechanistically insightful description of the vibrational relaxation and dissociation dynamics in rare gas--H$_2^+$/HD$^+$ complexes, linking initial approach geometry to final rotational state distributions and complex lifetimes, thereby probing the long-range part of the intermolecular interaction.

title: The disordered logistic map
summary: The logistic map is a quintessential model in the study of low-dimensional chaos. High-dimensional chaos, on the other hand, presents itself in disordered systems with many interacting and heterogeneously coupled components. Here, we formulate a system of many logistic maps, interacting through disordered couplings. Using a combination of dynamic mean-field theory, random matrix theory and numerical simulations, we show that even the smallest amount of disorder can remove the period-doubling cascade in the conventional logistic map. Instead we find a transition to high-dimensional chaos, marked by an oscillatory instability not previously reported for disordered systems. We also show that with sufficiently strong homogeneous coupling between the maps one recovers elements of the conventional period-doubling cascade. Our findings indicate that well-known phenomena in dynamical systems can be fragile in the face of disorder. At the same time, new phenomena emerge that are neither found in simple low-dimensional dynamics nor in high-dimensional disordered systems.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a system of many coupled logistic maps with disordered couplings, showing that even minimal disorder eliminates the period-doubling cascade and drives a transition to high-dimensional chaos via a novel oscillatory instability.
AI.motivation: The logistic map is a canonical model of low-dimensional chaos, while high-dimensional chaos typically arises in disordered systems with many interacting, heterogeneously coupled components. The authors aim to bridge these two regimes by asking how disorder affects the well-established phenomena of the logistic map.
AI.method: The authors formulate a system of many logistic maps interacting through disordered couplings. They combine dynamic mean-field theory, random matrix theory, and numerical simulations to analyze the collective dynamics across varying disorder and coupling strengths.
AI.result: Even the smallest amount of disorder removes the period-doubling cascade of the conventional logistic map, replacing it with a transition to high-dimensional chaos marked by an oscillatory instability not previously reported in disordered systems. With sufficiently strong homogeneous coupling, elements of the conventional period-doubling cascade are recovered.
AI.conclusion: Well-known phenomena in dynamical systems can be fragile under disorder, while simultaneously giving rise to new phenomena that appear neither in simple low-dimensional dynamics nor in high-dimensional disordered systems.

title: A subcell-refined entropy-residual-driven limiting strategy for high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods
summary: Fine-grained, subcell-level dissipation control is essential for achieving robust high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) simulations of nonlinear hyperbolic systems in under-resolved regimes while preserving accuracy. This paper proposes a subcell-refined entropy-residual-driven limiting strategy for DG on Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto nodes. The limiter introduces only nearest-neighbor pairwise dissipation within each element, with closed-form coefficients that supply the minimal dissipation required to restore the element entropy inequality. The strategy is a diagonal, locally stable approximation of classical entropy-stable methods, and a generalized subcell framework reveals split-form DG and residual-distribution-based entropy correction schemes as particular choices of the limiting coefficients. For the Euler equations, a physically consistent jump operator separately models thermal and shear entropy production while preserving velocity and pressure equilibrium; a subcell refinement of the Zhang-Shu positivity limiter ensures pointwise positivity. Extensive numerical tests confirm that the scheme maintains optimal high-order accuracy, strictly enforces entropy dissipation, and significantly reduces the difficulty of a posteriori positivity-preserving procedures.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a subcell-refined, entropy-residual-driven limiting strategy for DG schemes on Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto nodes, achieving minimal nearest-neighbor dissipation with closed-form coefficients while preserving optimal high-order accuracy.
AI.motivation: Robust high-order DG simulations of nonlinear hyperbolic systems in under-resolved regimes require fine-grained, subcell-level dissipation control that enforces entropy stability without sacrificing accuracy. Existing entropy-stable or limiting approaches often introduce excessive dissipation or are difficult to reconcile with accuracy preservation.
AI.method: The limiter applies only nearest-neighbor pairwise dissipation within each element, using closed-form coefficients that provide the minimal dissipation needed to restore the element entropy inequality. It is formulated as a diagonal, locally stable approximation of classical entropy-stable methods, and a generalized subcell framework shows split-form DG and residual-distribution-based entropy correction as special cases of the limiting coefficients. For the Euler equations, a physically consistent jump operator separately models thermal and shear entropy production while preserving velocity and pressure equilibrium; a subcell refinement of the Zhang-Shu positivity limiter guarantees pointwise positivity.
AI.result: Extensive numerical tests show the scheme maintains optimal high-order accuracy, strictly enforces entropy dissipation, and substantially reduces the difficulty of a posteriori positivity-preserving procedures.
AI.conclusion: The proposed subcell-refined entropy-residual-driven limiter offers a unified, minimally dissipative, and locally stable framework for entropy-stable DG discretizations of nonlinear hyperbolic systems, encompassing existing entropy correction schemes as particular cases while enabling robust under-resolved simulations.

title: Quantitative Dried droplet Morphology and Image Analysis for Screening Adulteration in Milk
summary: Adulteration of milk with water, urea, calcium compounds and starch is still a widespread food safety problem, especially in areas where there is no access to laboratory based chemical testing, and is a global threat to human food safety and security, especially for children and the elderly. We present the development of a reagent free screening method, based on droplet evaporative deposition method, optical microscopy, and quantitative image analysis, for consistent detection and classification of milk adulteration. Droplets of Single Toned ST, 3% fat, and Double Toned DT, 1.5% fat milk samples, adulterated with water, urea, calcium, and starch, respectively, at different concentrations were tested. Deposition patterns were characterized by image processing using radial intensity profile descriptors area under the curve, and edge decay slope and gray level co occurrence matrix GLCM texture features contrast, correlation, energy, homogeneity, and entropy. The descriptors exhibit consistent adulterant specific trends: water and urea adulteration resulted in increasingly smooth, more homogeneous deposits decreasing contrast, increasing homogeneity, while calcium and starch adulteration resulted in structurally rougher deposits increasing contrast, decreasing homogeneity. Urea was further distinguished in the two groups by a significant increase in homogeneity and entropy collapse at higher concentrations, whereas calcium and starch were distinguished by diverging area under curve AUC trends. Milk type ST vs. DT was resolved by a combined multivariate signature of the descriptors at baseline. Our findings show that a simple, two level feature based framework: first resolving milk type, then adulterant family, then specific adulterant identity can be realized entirely from optical microscopy data without additional chemical reagents.

AI.tldr: A reagent-free method combining droplet evaporative deposition, optical microscopy, and quantitative image analysis detects and classifies milk adulteration (water, urea, calcium, starch) and resolves milk type from deposit pattern features.
AI.motivation: Milk adulteration with water, urea, calcium compounds, and starch remains a widespread food safety problem, particularly where laboratory-based chemical testing is unavailable, posing a global threat to food safety and security, especially for children and the elderly.
AI.method: Droplets of Single Toned (3% fat) and Double Toned (1.5% fat) milk adulterated with water, urea, calcium, and starch at varying concentrations were analyzed via droplet evaporative deposition and optical microscopy. Deposition patterns were characterized using radial intensity profile descriptors (area under the curve, edge decay slope) and gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features (contrast, correlation, energy, homogeneity, entropy).
AI.result: Descriptors showed consistent adulterant-specific trends: water and urea produced smooth, homogeneous deposits (decreasing contrast, increasing homogeneity), while calcium and starch produced rougher deposits (increasing contrast, decreasing homogeneity). Urea was distinguished by increased homogeneity and entropy collapse at higher concentrations; calcium and starch by diverging AUC trends. Milk type (ST vs. DT) was resolved via a combined multivariate descriptor signature at baseline.
AI.conclusion: A simple two-level feature-based framework—first resolving milk type, then adulterant family, then specific adulterant identity—can be realized entirely from optical microscopy data without additional chemical reagents.

title: Detection of signals in presence of noise through Josephson junction switching currents
summary: Josephson junctions can be employed to reveal a sinusoidal signal in presence of Gaussian noise. To mimic realistic setups, the detection is performed linearly ramping the bias current until a switch to the finite voltage occurs; the analysis of the resulting switching currents can be exploited to decide about the presence of the harmonic drive. The signal is applied in two conditions: with an unknown initial phase (incoherent strategy) and with a known initial phase (coherent strategy). In both conditions, the analysis of the efficiency of the detection, performed through the signal-to-noise ratio, as estimated by the Kumar-Carrol index, shows that the dependence upon the Josephson junction ramp rate is beneficial, especially for relatively fast speed. One can conclude that the collection of the switching currents is a robust technique, and thus it is possible to exploit the advantages of a predetermined finite time to collect the data.

AI.tldr: Josephson junctions are used to detect a sinusoidal signal buried in Gaussian noise via linearly ramped bias currents; analyzing switching currents (via the Kumar-Carrol SNR index) shows that a faster ramp rate improves detection efficiency for both incoherent and coherent phase strategies.
AI.motivation: Realistic detection setups do not use ideal continuous measurements; instead, the bias current is ramped until the junction switches to finite voltage. There is a need to assess whether this switching-current-based detection is robust and how the ramp rate affects sensitivity when deciding about the presence of a harmonic drive.
AI.method: A Josephson junction is subjected to a sinusoidal signal plus Gaussian noise. The bias current is linearly ramped until switching to finite voltage occurs, and the resulting switching currents are collected for statistical analysis. Two conditions are compared: an unknown initial phase (incoherent strategy) and a known initial phase (coherent strategy). Detection efficiency is quantified by the signal-to-noise ratio estimated through the Kumar-Carrol index.
AI.result: In both coherent and incoherent conditions, detection efficiency depends on the Josephson junction ramp rate, and this dependence is beneficial, particularly at relatively fast speeds. Faster ramping yields improved SNR as estimated by the Kumar-Carrol index.
AI.conclusion: Collecting switching currents is a robust detection technique. Because the ramp-rate dependence is favorable, one can exploit the advantages of a predetermined finite time to collect the data, enabling efficient signal detection with practical, time-bounded measurements.

title: Non-Hermitian Quantum Mechanics I: Instantaneous Self-Energy
summary: Starting from the unitary evolution of a closed quantum system, we rigorously demonstrate that the projection of the global wavefunction onto an arbitrary local subsystem is governed by an exact, time-dependent non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation. Crucially, the derivation does not rely on conventional approximations such as the Born approximation, the Markov approximation, or the wide-band limit. The central quantity is the \textit{instantaneous self-energy}, a time-dependent and generally non-Hermitian operator that encodes environmental backaction and, together with the subsystem Hamiltonian, forms the exact time-local generator of the projected dynamics. By benchmarking the conventional non-Hermitian approximation against this exact framework, we systematically expose its limitations. These results provide a rigorous microscopic foundation for the emergence of effective non-Hermitian dynamics in quantum systems.

AI.tldr: The paper derives an exact time-dependent non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation for the projected (local subsystem) dynamics of a closed quantum system, requiring no Born, Markov, or wide-band approximations, and benchmarks the conventional non-Hermitian approximation against this exact framework.
AI.motivation: Effective non-Hermitian dynamics in quantum systems are typically justified only under restrictive approximations (Born, Markov, wide-band limit). A rigorous, approximation-free microscopic foundation for their emergence was lacking.
AI.method: Starting from unitary evolution of a closed quantum system, the global wavefunction is projected onto an arbitrary local subsystem. The resulting exact, time-local generator is constructed from the subsystem Hamiltonian plus a newly identified instantaneous self-energy — a time-dependent, generally non-Hermitian operator encoding environmental backaction.
AI.result: The projected dynamics obey an exact, time-dependent non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation, derived without Born, Markov, or wide-band approximations. Benchmarking the conventional non-Hermitian approximation against this exact framework systematically reveals its limitations.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a rigorous microscopic foundation for the emergence of effective non-Hermitian dynamics in quantum systems and clarifies the validity and shortcomings of standard non-Hermitian approximations.

title: The ferromagnetic diatomic molecules with the mixed spin-1/2 and spin-1
summary: Diatomic molecules consisting of one spin-1/2 ($σ$) and one spin-1 ($S$) atom are put at each site of the Bethe lattice (BL) of the coordination number $q=3, 4$, or 6. Alongside the ferromagnetic (FM) interactions of individual atoms within a molecule, the molecules are permitted to engage in ferromagnetic interactions with their nearest neighbors (NN) through diverse bilinear interaction parameters $J$. The spin-1 sites are also under the influence of crystal field $D$. The phase diagrams on the ($D, T$) planes for a given $q$ are obtained by investigating the thermal variations of magnetizations for the case with zero external magnetic field $(H)$. It is discovered that the phase diagrams rely on $q$ both qualitatively and quantitatively. The crystal field is also included which operates only on the spin-1 sites. Three separate FM phases are observed with ($σ,S$) being $(1/2,1), (1/2,0)$ at the ground state level and a phase region with small magnetization (SM) values at a higher temperature range. In addition to the reentrant behavior in the transition zone from one phase to the other, the model produces first- and second-order phase transitions. Additionally, the impact of $H$ on the magnetization curves is examined, yielding quite intriguing findings.

AI.tldr: Mixed-spin (σ=1/2, S=1) diatomic molecules on Bethe lattices (q=3,4,6) with intra- and inter-molecular ferromagnetic couplings and crystal field D exhibit q-dependent phase diagrams featuring three FM phases, reentrant behavior, and first/second-order transitions.
AI.motivation: To investigate how lattice coordination number q and crystal field D influence the magnetic phase behavior of a mixed-spin diatomic molecular system, extending earlier studies on such molecule-based spin models.
AI.method: Diatomic molecules (one spin-1/2 σ, one spin-1 S) placed on Bethe lattices of q=3,4,6 with intra-molecular and nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic bilinear interactions J, spin-1 sites subject to crystal field D. Phase diagrams in the (D,T) plane obtained via thermal variation of magnetizations at zero and finite external field H.
AI.result: Phase diagrams depend on q qualitatively and quantitatively. Three distinct FM phases arise, with (σ,S)=(1/2,1) and (1/2,0) at ground state and a small-magnetization (SM) region at higher temperatures. Both first- and second-order transitions occur, along with reentrant behavior. External field H produces intriguing effects on magnetization curves.
AI.conclusion: The mixed-spin diatomic molecular model on Bethe lattices reveals rich, q-dependent phase topology with multiple FM phases, reentrance, and mixed-order transitions, highlighting the interplay of coordination number, crystal field, and magnetic field.

title: Hund-driven local-itinerant duality of Eu-4$f$ electrons in infinite-layer nickelates
summary: Recent discovery of reentrant superconductivity and elevated $T_c$ in Eu-substituted infinite-layer nickelates raises a critical question concerning the nature of Eu-4$f$ states and their potential interaction with Ni-$d$ electrons. Here we combine density functional theory with the dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) calculations to investigate the valence and magnetic properties of Eu-ions in the nickelate 112 structure, explicitly treating the Coulomb repulsion in both Ni-3$d$ and Eu-4$f$ shells. We find a three-regime evolution of the Eu-4$f$ configuration driven by its Hund's rule coupling $J_{\rm H}$. The magnetic and mixed-valence Eu ionic state inferred by experiments only occurs for moderate $J_{\rm H}$, with coexisting local moments and strongly correlated $j=7/2$ quasiparticles, in contrast to the nonmagnetic state at small $J_{\rm H}$ and the fully spin-polarized divalent state at large $J_{\rm H}$. This local-itinerant duality arises from an effectively hole-doped orbital-selective Mott state induced by the intra-4$f$ charge transfer between $j=5/2$ and $7/2$ manifolds. It not only explains the origin of the mixed-valence and local moment behaviors of the Eu-ions observed experimentally, but also predicts low-energy 4$f$ quasiparticles that may hybridize with the Ni-3$d$ electrons and contribute to the elevated $T_c$. Our work provides a basis for understanding the unusual ferromagnetic and superconducting properties of Eu-substituted infinite-layer nickelates.

AI.tldr: DFT+DMFT calculations reveal a three-regime evolution of Eu-4f states in Eu-substituted infinite-layer nickelates controlled by Hund's coupling J_H, explaining the mixed-valence/local-moment Eu behavior and predicting low-energy 4f quasiparticles that may hybridize with Ni-3d electrons and boost Tc.
AI.motivation: Reentrant superconductivity and elevated Tc in Eu-substituted infinite-layer nickelates raise the question of the nature of Eu-4f states and how they interact with Ni-3d electrons. Understanding the valence and magnetic character of Eu is key to explaining the unusual ferromagnetic and superconducting properties.
AI.method: The authors combine density functional theory with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT), explicitly treating Coulomb repulsion in both the Ni-3d and Eu-4f shells in the nickelate 112 structure, and study how the Eu-4f configuration depends on the Hund's rule coupling J_H.
AI.result: A three-regime evolution of the Eu-4f configuration emerges: nonmagnetic at small J_H, a magnetic mixed-valence ionic state at moderate J_H (with coexisting local moments and strongly correlated j=7/2 quasiparticles), and a fully spin-polarized divalent state at large J_H. The moderate-J_H local-itinerant duality originates from an effectively hole-doped orbital-selective Mott state induced by intra-4f charge transfer between the j=5/2 and j=7/2 manifolds.
AI.conclusion: The calculations reproduce the experimentally observed mixed-valence and local-moment behaviors of Eu ions and predict low-energy 4f quasiparticles that may hybridize with Ni-3d electrons and contribute to the elevated Tc, providing a basis for understanding the ferromagnetic and superconducting properties of Eu-substituted infinite-layer nickelates.

title: Laser-Ablated Au Electrodes with Preferred Orientation and Flat Interface on Oxides
summary: Gold (Au) thin-film electrodes deposited on oxides by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) exhibit distinctive structural properties compared with thermally evaporated Au films. While thermally evaporated Au forms polycrystalline films with randomly oriented grains, PLD-grown Au films show a strong preferred [111] orientation perpendicular to the substrate surface, likely due to the energetic nature of the laser-ablated Au plume. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals atomically flat interfaces between the PLD-grown Au electrodes and epitaxial oxide thin films, separated by nanometer-scale gaps comparable to interlayer spacings in van der Waals materials. The highly ordered microstructure and flat interfacial morphology result in enhanced adhesion of the Au films to oxide surfaces. These results demonstrate that PLD can produce both high-quality Au electrodes and oxide thin films within a single deposition platform, offering improved interfacial control and potential benefits for a wide range of oxide electronic and functional devices.

AI.tldr: PLD-grown Au thin films on oxides exhibit strong [111] preferred orientation and atomically flat interfaces with epitaxial oxides, enabling high-quality electrodes and oxide films in a single deposition platform.
AI.motivation: Thermally evaporated Au films on oxides form randomly oriented polycrystalline grains with less controlled interfaces, limiting interfacial quality. The authors aim to obtain Au electrodes with better structural order and interfacial control for oxide electronic and functional devices.
AI.method: Au thin-film electrodes were deposited on oxides by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) and compared with thermally evaporated Au films. Structural characterization included orientation analysis and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) to examine grain orientation and Au/oxide interface morphology.
AI.result: PLD-grown Au films show a strong preferred [111] orientation perpendicular to the substrate, unlike randomly oriented thermally evaporated films, likely due to the energetic laser-ablated Au plume. HRTEM reveals atomically flat interfaces between PLD-grown Au and epitaxial oxide thin films, separated by nanometer-scale gaps comparable to interlayer spacings in van der Waals materials. The ordered microstructure and flat interface enhance Au adhesion to oxide surfaces.
AI.conclusion: PLD can produce both high-quality Au electrodes and oxide thin films within a single deposition platform, offering improved interfacial control and potential benefits for oxide electronic and functional devices.

title: Attosecond charge migration timescales are dominated by transition dipoles, not correlations
summary: Attosecond charge migration (CM) is an ultrafast process occurring when a molecule is irradiated by ultrashort laser pulses, creating a localized hole. The hole propagates rapidly through the molecule, generating electric currents and transferring charge across the molecular backbone. CM is a key ingredient in solar energy conversion, photosynthesis, and radiation damage. Despite its importance and intensive research, the fundamental physical and chemical mechanisms of CM remain not fully understood. Especially, a deeper insight into the role correlations play in the dynamics, and which chemical attributes determine CM timescales, is needed. Here we study with \textit{ab-initio} time-dependent density functional theory CM in the benchmark molecule, BrC$_4$H. We thoroughly explore CM under different initial conditions at the electronic and structural levels, including with theories of varying degrees of electronic correlations. We uncover a universal behavior where the hole moment (connecting to experimental observables) dominant frequency is roughly independent of all of these characteristics. In contrast, the timescales of the hole density evolution do vary with the chemical conditions and level of correlations. Employing a semi-analytical theory that reconstructs the hole moments in the cationic reference frame, we show that the attosecond timescale of CM is determined by molecular dipoles that filter out specific frequency responses with an analogy to optical selection rules. Our results provide essential insight into CM physics, which should be useful for interpreting attosecond experiments and engineering CM timescales by tailoring transition dipoles.

AI.tldr: This work uses ab-initio time-dependent density functional theory to study attosecond charge migration (CM) in BrC4H under varying initial conditions and levels of electronic correlation. It finds a universal behavior: the dominant frequency of the hole moment is roughly independent of these conditions, while the timescales of hole density evolution do vary. A semi-analytical theory shows that CM attosecond timescales are set by molecular dipoles acting like optical selection rules.
AI.motivation: Charge migration is central to solar energy conversion, photosynthesis, and radiation damage, yet its fundamental mechanisms remain poorly understood. In particular, the role of electronic correlations and the chemical attributes determining CM timescales require deeper insight.
AI.method: Ab-initio time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) is applied to the benchmark molecule BrC4H. The study systematically explores CM under different initial conditions at electronic and structural levels, using theories of varying degrees of electronic correlation. A semi-analytical theory is employed to reconstruct hole moments in the cationic reference frame.
AI.result: A universal behavior is uncovered: the dominant frequency of the hole moment (linked to experimental observables) is roughly independent of initial conditions, structure, and correlation level. In contrast, the timescales of hole density evolution do vary with chemical conditions and correlation level. The attosecond timescale of CM is shown to be determined by molecular dipoles that filter specific frequency responses, analogous to optical selection rules.
AI.conclusion: The results provide essential insight into CM physics, useful for interpreting attosecond experiments and for engineering CM timescales by tailoring transition dipoles.

title: Polar vibrational excitations and glass-like response in relaxor PMN
summary: Relaxor ferroelectrics retain crystalline order while exhibiting glass-like dielectric and thermal responses. Using atomistic models trained on first-principles data, we investigate these responses in the prototypical relaxor Pb(Mg_{1/3}Nb_{2/3})O_3 (PMN). Compositional disorder couples elastic motion to electric polarization, producing a continuum of polar vibrational excitations, unlike the discrete polar optical modes of conventional ferroelectric PbTiO_3. The simulations qualitatively reproduce the temperature dependence of the low-frequency susceptibility, while the calculated far-infrared spectra agree closely with experiments. At low frequencies, disorder in PMN generates a boson peak comprising excess phonon-like modes and quasi-localized excitations. The latter exhibit a quartic frequency dependence of their density of states and pronounced anharmonicity, as in structural glasses. These excess modes account for PMN's anomalous behavior in the specific heat for temperature higher than 5 K. These results connect the dielectric, optical, and thermal anomalies of a crystalline relaxor through its disorder-induced polar excitation spectrum.

AI.tldr: Atomistic simulations of Pb(Mg_{1/3}Nb_{2/3})O_3 reveal that compositional disorder produces a continuum of polar vibrational excitations and a boson peak, connecting the relaxor's dielectric, optical, and thermal anomalies.
AI.motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics retain crystalline order yet show glass-like dielectric and thermal responses, and the microscopic origin linking these anomalous behaviors remains inadequately understood.
AI.method: First-principles-trained atomistic models were used to study PMN, analyzing how compositional disorder couples elastic motion to electric polarization and computing polar vibrational spectra, low-frequency susceptibility, far-infrared spectra, and specific heat.
AI.result: Disorder yields a continuum of polar vibrational excitations rather than discrete polar optical modes (as in PbTiO_3). Simulations reproduce the temperature dependence of low-frequency susceptibility and agree closely with far-infrared experiments. A boson peak arises from excess phonon-like modes and quasi-localized excitations showing quartic frequency dependence of density of states and pronounced anharmonicity, accounting for the anomalous specific heat above 5 K.
AI.conclusion: The dielectric, optical, and thermal anomalies of crystalline PMN are unified through a disorder-induced polar excitation spectrum, explaining its glass-like behavior despite crystalline order.

title: VNS Tokamak for Medical Isotope Production
summary: The Volumetric Neutron Source (VNS) tokamak is a proposed fusion reactor for testing components under fusion neutron irradiation, and has potential use for radioisotope production. The VNS geometry is modeled in the Serpent 2.2.2 and OpenMC 0.15.2 neutronics codes. Coupled neutron-photon simulations compared fluxes, spectra, and selected reaction rates in the blanket and vacuum vessel. Good agreement was found overall, with the largest difference found in (n, 2n) reactions. On an HPC cluster, Serpent 2 was found to have shorter computation time in coupled simulations, while OpenMC was faster in neutron only simulations. Radioisotope production yields were simulated in Serpent 2.2.2 for capsule and Cobalt plate irradiation facilities. Results indicate potential for large volume production of 99Mo, 131I, 225Ac, 177Lu, 192Ir, 64Cu, 67Cu, 161Tb, and 153Sm while 203Pb indicates lower potential. 100Mo and LEU target heating was calculated, suggesting the LEU target mass or the cooling may need adjustment. Optimized 60Co production yielded 1.2 GBq/mg and 100,000 TBq after a 3-year irradiation period. Sensitivity to plant outage for 99Mo, 131I, 177Lu, and 60Co was simulated, suggesting irradiation can be restarted for the same isotope loading and demonstrated long-lived 60Co to be robust to long plant dwell-time.

AI.tldr: A coupled neutron-photon neutronic model of the VNS tokamak was benchmarked between Serpent 2.2.2 and OpenMC 0.15.2, showing good agreement and code-dependent performance; Serpent 2 simulations indicate strong potential for large-volume medical radioisotope production, with LEU target heating flagged as a design constraint and 60Co production proving robust to plant outages.
AI.motivation: The Volumetric Neutron Source (VNS) tokamak is proposed as a fusion reactor for testing components under fusion neutron irradiation and has potential for radioisotope production. A validated neutronic model is needed both to support the irradiation-testing mission and to assess the feasibility of isotope production in this geometry.
AI.method: The VNS geometry was modeled in Serpent 2.2.2 and OpenMC 0.15.2. Coupled neutron-photon simulations compared fluxes, spectra, and selected reaction rates in the blanket and vacuum vessel. Computation times were benchmarked on an HPC cluster. Radioisotope production yields were then simulated in Serpent 2.2.2 for capsule and Cobalt plate irradiation facilities, including 100Mo and LEU target heating, optimized 60Co production, and sensitivity to plant outage for 99Mo, 131I, 177Lu, and 60Co.
AI.result: Good overall agreement was found between the two codes, with the largest discrepancy in (n, 2n) reactions. On the HPC cluster, Serpent 2 had shorter computation time in coupled simulations, while OpenMC was faster in neutron-only simulations. Simulations indicate potential for large-volume production of 99Mo, 131I, 225Ac, 177Lu, 192Ir, 64Cu, 67Cu, 161Tb, and 153Sm, whereas 203Pb shows lower potential. 100Mo and LEU target heating calculations suggest the LEU target mass or cooling may need adjustment. Optimized 60Co production yielded 1.2 GBq/mg and 100,000 TBq after a 3-year irradiation period. Outage sensitivity simulations suggest irradiation can be restarted for the same isotope loading, and long-lived 60Co is robust to long plant dwell-time.
AI.conclusion: The VNS neutronic model is cross-validated across two independent Monte Carlo codes, with code performance depending on whether photon transport is coupled. The geometry supports large-volume production of several medically relevant radioisotopes, though LEU target heating requires design adjustment. 60Co production is optimized and robust to plant outages, supporting the VNS as a viable multi-purpose irradiation facility.

title: Pendellösung length-scale neutron and X-ray interferometry
summary: Neutron and X-ray perfect-crystal interferometers (PCIs) are powerful platforms for studies of fundamental physics and phase-contrast imaging. Further enhancing several PCI capabilities requires reducing crystal blade thickness to the micron scale, which minimizes dynamical-diffraction image blur, permits operation in the pendellösung regime where blade thickness controls beam splitting, and reduces absorption for simultaneous neutron and X-ray operation. However, fabricating multiple crystal blades with identical micrometer-scale thicknesses over centimeter-scale areas remains a major challenge. Here, using a non-etching sub-micron fabrication technique, we demonstrate silicon triple-Laue interferometers with equal-blade-thicknesses of 110 $μ$m and 350 $μ$m, operated with both neutrons and X-rays. These devices are the thinnest PCIs realized to date, enabling a factor-of-six reduction in dynamical-diffraction beam spreading for improved phase-contrast imaging, while reaching the single pendellösung length regime in which crystal thickness provides an experimentally accessible control parameter for engineered quantum-optical beam splitting of plane-wave inputs. These results motivate multi-blade PCI designs utilizing identical half-pendellösung crystal lamellae that are proposed for neutron spin--orbit and electric dipole moment measurements.

AI.tldr: Using a non-etching sub-micron fabrication technique, the authors demonstrate silicon triple-Laue interferometers with equal blade thicknesses of 110 μm and 350 μm, operated with both neutrons and X-rays—the thinnest perfect-crystal interferometers to date.
AI.motivation: Perfect-crystal interferometers (PCIs) are powerful platforms for fundamental physics and phase-contrast imaging, but enhancing their capabilities requires reducing crystal blade thickness to the micron scale to minimize dynamical-diffraction image blur, enable pendellösung-regime operation, and reduce absorption for simultaneous neutron and X-ray use. Fabricating multiple identical micrometer-scale blades over centimeter-scale areas, however, remains a major challenge.
AI.method: A non-etching sub-micron fabrication technique was used to produce silicon triple-Laue interferometers with equal blade thicknesses of 110 μm and 350 μm.
AI.result: The devices are the thinnest PCIs realized to date, enabling a factor-of-six reduction in dynamical-diffraction beam spreading for improved phase-contrast imaging and reaching the single pendellösung length regime, where crystal thickness serves as an experimentally accessible control parameter for engineered quantum-optical beam splitting of plane-wave inputs. They were operated with both neutrons and X-rays.
AI.conclusion: These results motivate multi-blade PCI designs using identical half-pendellösung crystal lamellae, proposed for neutron spin–orbit and electric dipole moment measurements.

title: New theoretical model of the dynamic anomalies in HTc superconductors
summary: New theoretical model of the dynamic current-voltage characteristics anomalies in HTc superconductors in slowly varying magnetic field has been proposed. The model is based on an analysis in details of the magnetic flux penetration into HTc superconducting slab in such case. The comparison of model with previous experimental data has been presented. Theoretical analysis resulting from a new solution of diffusion equation is given as well as other one based on phenomenological critical state model.

AI.tldr: A new theoretical model explains dynamic current-voltage (I-V) anomalies in high-temperature (HTc) superconductors under a slowly varying magnetic field, based on detailed magnetic flux penetration into a superconducting slab, and is compared with prior experimental data.
AI.motivation: Dynamic current-voltage characteristics in HTc superconductors exhibit anomalies under slowly varying magnetic fields that require a theoretical explanation grounded in the underlying flux penetration physics.
AI.method: Detailed analysis of magnetic flux penetration into an HTc superconducting slab, combining a new solution of the diffusion equation with a phenomenological critical state model.
AI.result: The proposed model reproduces and is compared against previous experimental data on dynamic I-V anomalies.
AI.conclusion: The new diffusion-equation solution and critical-state-based approach together provide a consistent theoretical account of the observed dynamic I-V anomalies in HTc superconductors.

title: Sub-Thermionic Switching in a Negative-Capacitance Bandgap-Change Field-Effect Transistor
comment: 9 pages 4 figures. Also includes Supplementary Material with 5 figures
summary: Overcoming the approximately 60~mV/dec Boltzmann limit of the subthreshold swing remains a central challenge for low-power nanoelectronics. Negative-capacitance field-effect transistors address it by amplifying the channel potential, but their effectiveness is constrained by capacitance matching and by the quantum capacitance of conventional channels. Here we model a negative-capacitance bandgap-change field-effect transistor (NC-BCFET), in which the ferroelectric gate stack instead amplifies the electric field that opens the bandgap of the channel, using experimentally proven materials: bilayer graphene as a channel with an electrically tunable bandgap and Al$_{0.55}$Sc$_{0.45}$N as the negative-capacitance ferroelectric. Our self-consistent framework couples a four-band tight-binding Hamiltonian with GW-corrected screening, a quasistatic Landau--Devonshire ferroelectric response, and ballistic Landauer--Büttiker transport. Negative capacitance amplifies the interlayer potential difference, compressing the switching window 37-fold relative to a dielectric-gated control. At 300~K, the optimized NC-BCFET achieves a subthreshold swing of 15~mV/dec, four times below the Boltzmann limit, improving to 2.5~mV/dec at 100~K. The room-temperature on/off ratio is limited to $\sim 10^{2}$ by the bandgap of bilayer graphene. The concept extends directly to materials with larger field-tunable bandgaps, where deep subthermionic switching and high on/off ratios can be achieved together at room temperature.

AI.tldr: The paper models a negative-capacitance bandgap-change FET using bilayer graphene (tunable-gap channel) and AlScN ferroelectric, achieving subthreshold swings of 15 mV/dec at 300 K (2.5 mV/dec at 100 K) via field-driven bandgap opening, though limited to ~10^2 on/off ratio by the small bilayer-graphene gap.
AI.motivation: Overcoming the ~60 mV/dec Boltzmann limit of subthreshold swing is a central challenge for low-power nanoelectronics. Negative-capacitance FETs amplify channel potential but their effectiveness is constrained by capacitance matching and the quantum capacitance of conventional channels, motivating an alternative mechanism.
AI.method: A negative-capacitance bandgap-change FET (NC-BCFET) is modeled, in which the ferroelectric gate stack amplifies the electric field that opens the channel bandgap, using experimentally proven materials: bilayer graphene (electrically tunable bandgap) and Al0.55Sc0.45N (negative-capacitance ferroelectric). A self-consistent framework couples a four-band tight-binding Hamiltonian with GW-corrected screening, a quasistatic Landau-Devonshire ferroelectric response, and ballistic Landauer-Buttiker transport.
AI.result: Negative capacitance amplifies the interlayer potential difference, compressing the switching window 37-fold relative to a dielectric-gated control. At 300 K the optimized NC-BCFET achieves a subthreshold swing of 15 mV/dec, four times below the Boltzmann limit, improving to 2.5 mV/dec at 100 K. The room-temperature on/off ratio is limited to ~10^2 by the bilayer graphene bandgap.
AI.conclusion: The concept extends directly to materials with larger field-tunable bandgaps, where deep subthermionic switching and high on/off ratios can be achieved together at room temperature.

title: A Spatio-Temporal Generalisation of Green Kubo
comment: 41 pages (double spaced), 14 Figures, pre-final checks draft
summary: The Green-Kubo (GK) method which is used to obtain the shear viscosity of a model liquid in equilibrium molecular dynamics (MD) often requires long simulation times to obtain acceptable statistics. This work extends the GK approach to include spatial correlations. The total shear stress in the GK expression is split into a grid of its components in contiguous volumes. In doing this, the autocorrelation of the total system stress can be rewritten as the cross-correlation of the subvolume stresses. This provides a novel real-space insight into the liquid structure, something previously only treated in Fourier space by liquid-state theory. A novel travelling wave like structure is exposed that is shown to be well fitted by a leading Gaussian pulse added to a second negative Gaussian for the bounce back. The fitting parameters include the wave position, magnitude and width which show deep insights into the liquid property. The wave moves at the speed of sound over short times before decreasing in speed with the square root of time, while the wave packet spreads out also as the square root of time. The magnitude is decreasing with form $t^{-3/2}$, a result with strong significance in the history of MD simulation. These fitted forms mean the entire spatial temporal response of the liquid can be modelled in closed form by fitting to data, with short term requiring MD and the long time and distances approximated by the Gaussian form. By limiting the correlation to localized interactions the longer range contribution, which essentially only contribute to the noise, can be eliminated. This looks like a promising approach to model viscosity by taking short MD runs and fitting the long time behaviour.

AI.tldr: The Green-Kubo (GK) method for computing shear viscosity in equilibrium MD is extended to include spatial correlations by decomposing the total stress into subvolume stress components, revealing a travelling-wave-like real-space structure in the stress autocorrelation that can be fitted in closed form.
AI.motivation: Standard GK shear-viscosity calculations require prohibitively long simulation times to achieve acceptable statistics. The authors aim to reduce this cost and simultaneously gain real-space insight into liquid structure and dynamics, which previously had only been accessible in Fourier space via liquid-state theory.
AI.method: The total shear stress in the GK expression is split over a grid of contiguous subvolumes. The autocorrelation of the total system stress is then rewritten as a cross-correlation of subvolume stresses, yielding a spatially resolved (real-space) correlation function. The resulting spatiotemporal response is characterized by fitting: a leading Gaussian pulse plus a second negative Gaussian representing the bounce-back. Fitting parameters (wave position, magnitude, width) are extracted and analyzed.
AI.result: A novel travelling-wave-like structure is exposed and well fitted by the two-Gaussian model. The wave travels at the speed of sound at short times, then decelerates as the square root of time; the wave packet spreads as the square root of time; and its magnitude decays as t^{-3/2}. Limiting the correlation to localized interactions removes the longer-range contributions that mainly add noise.
AI.conclusion: The entire spatiotemporal response of the liquid can be modelled in closed form by fitting to data, with short times requiring MD and long times/distances approximated by the Gaussian form. This offers a promising route to model viscosity using short MD runs plus fitting of the long-time behaviour.

title: Electronic structure and anisotropic magnetotransport in the topological kagome ferromagnet MgMn6Sn6
summary: We report the magnetic, magnetotransport, and electronic properties of the kagome ferromag net MgMn6Sn6 using magnetization, angle dependent magnetoresistance, x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD), angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), and first-principles cal culations. MgMn6Sn6 exhibits ferromagnetic ordering near TC=295 K with pronounced easy plane magnetic anisotropy. At low temperatures and low magnetic fields, the magnetoresistance (MR) is strongly anisotropic with respect to the magnetic field orientation, evolving from a predominantly negative MR for in-plane fields to a more quadratic behavior for out-of-plane fields. Angle depen dent measurements further reveal a pronounced twofold MR anisotropy with additional higher order contributions. The finite orbital-to-spin moment ratio revealed by XMCD suggests a significant role of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in MgMn6Sn6. The first-principles calculations show a Dirac-like band crossing at the K point and a van Hove singularity (VHS) at the M point, as expected for kagome materials. ARPES measurements resolve a sixfold symmetric Fermi surface and its systematic evo lution with binding energy, in overall agreement with first-principles calculations. The measured band dispersions are also broadly consistent with the calculated multiband electronic structure. These results establish the connection between magnetic anisotropy, anisotropic magnetotransport, and the kagome derived electronic structure of MgMn6Sn6.

AI.tldr: MgMn6Sn6 is a kagome ferromagnet (TC ≈ 295 K) with easy-plane anisotropy; its anisotropic magnetotransport is linked to SOC and kagome-derived band features (Dirac crossing, van Hove singularity), confirmed by XMCD, ARPES, and first-principles calculations.
AI.motivation: To establish the connection between magnetic anisotropy, anisotropic magnetotransport, and the kagome-derived electronic structure in the kagome ferromagnet MgMn6Sn6.
AI.method: Magnetization, angle-dependent magnetoresistance, X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD), angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), and first-principles calculations.
AI.result: MgMn6Sn6 orders ferromagnetically near TC = 295 K with pronounced easy-plane anisotropy. Low-temperature, low-field MR is strongly field-orientation dependent, evolving from predominantly negative (in-plane fields) to more quadratic (out-of-plane fields), with twofold anisotropy plus higher-order contributions. XMCD reveals a finite orbital-to-spin moment ratio indicating significant SOC. Calculations show a Dirac-like band crossing at K and a van Hove singularity at M; ARPES resolves a sixfold symmetric Fermi surface and binding-energy evolution consistent with calculations.
AI.conclusion: The results establish the connection between magnetic anisotropy, anisotropic magnetotransport, and the kagome-derived electronic structure of MgMn6Sn6.

title: Mobility-lifetime relation links photodegradation in spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells
summary: The degradation mechanisms of organic solar cells (OSCs) have been studied primarily in spin-coated, laboratory-scale devices, whereas scalable processing modifies the device architecture, active-layer morphology, and underlying charge-transport and recombination properties. Whether these changes also alter how solar cells degrade remains unclear. Here, we compare spin-coated and fully roll-to-roll-compatible gravure-printed PM6:Y12 solar cells during $\sim$1000 h of continuous illumination. Despite distinct initial properties and degradation signatures, the loss of power-conversion efficiency systematically follows the mobility-lifetime product $μτ$. Remarkably, ageing of the printed devices increases the recombination lifetime while strongly reducing charge-carrier mobility, showing that a longer lifetime alone does not imply improved device performance. The mobility reduction is accompanied by decreased PM6 lamellar order, whereas the additional open-circuit voltage loss originates predominantly from increased non-radiative recombination. Dark recovery further reveals a metastable contribution specific to the printed architecture. These results identify the mobility-lifetime product as a unifying physical descriptor for photodegradation, linking ageing-induced microscopic changes to macroscopic performance loss across spin-coated and scalable printed OSCs.

AI.tldr: This study compares spin-coated and gravure-printed PM6:Y12 organic solar cells over ~1000 h of illumination, showing that efficiency loss in both tracks universally tracks the mobility-lifetime product (μτ), that printing-specific ageing raises lifetime yet lowers mobility, and that μτ serves as a unifying descriptor of photodegradation.
AI.motivation: Degradation studies of organic solar cells have largely relied on spin-coated, laboratory-scale devices. Scalable processing, however, changes device architecture, active-layer morphology, and charge-transport/recombination behavior, so it is unclear whether degradation mechanisms established for spin-coated cells also apply to printed, industrially relevant devices. This gap motivates a direct comparison of degradation pathways across the two processing routes.
AI.method: Spin-coated and fully roll-to-roll-compatible gravure-printed PM6:Y12 solar cells were aged under ~1000 h of continuous illumination. Their initial properties and degradation signatures were compared, with emphasis on charge-transport and recombination parameters such as carrier mobility, recombination lifetime, and the mobility-lifetime product (μτ). Microstructural order (PM6 lamellar order) and non-radiative recombination losses were examined, and dark recovery measurements probed metastable contributions specific to the printed architecture.
AI.result: Despite distinct initial properties and degradation signatures, power-conversion-efficiency loss systematically followed μτ in both device types. Ageing of printed devices increased the recombination lifetime while strongly reducing charge-carrier mobility, demonstrating that longer lifetime alone does not guarantee better performance. The mobility decrease coincided with reduced PM6 lamellar order, while additional open-circuit voltage loss arose predominantly from increased non-radiative recombination. Dark recovery revealed a metastable contribution unique to the printed architecture.
AI.conclusion: The mobility-lifetime product μτ is identified as a unifying physical descriptor for photodegradation, linking ageing-induced microscopic changes to macroscopic performance loss across both spin-coated and scalable printed organic solar cells. This provides a processing-independent metric for assessing and predicting degradation in OSCs.

title: AI-assisted analytical theory in soft matter and multiphysics: new results and lessons from diffusiophoresis and bipolar membranes
summary: We present a framework to advance analytical theory in the area of soft matter and multiphysics using assistance from AI. The framework emphasizes (i) setting "honesty rules", (ii) focusing on a few key papers that are used to formulate a problem of interest, (iii) specifying checks a priori, (iv) using only one task per session and keeping a running log of tasks, checks, corrections, and sessions so that a mistake is not propagated through a project, and (v) ensuring all decisions are approved by humans while AI focuses primarily on execution. The framework is applied to two distinct problems to create new knowledge, including (i) diffusiophoresis of a spherical particle in the presence of an arbitrary number of electrolytes at arbitrary Debye lengths, and (ii) analytical description of I-V curves, including overlimiting current, in bipolar membranes without including the water dissociation kinetics. Both of these problems are advanced analyses and would each typically require several months to a year's worth of effort, but were solved in a matter of a few days. However, the increased efficiency should be cautiously navigated to avoid cognitive offloading and ensure that AI-assisted results are used to extract human-readable insights instead of just reporting a new mathematical formula. The usage of AI is transparently presented. Finally, we also share brief thoughts on how to integrate AI tools in theoretical research during graduate education.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an AI-assisted framework for advancing analytical theory in soft matter and multiphysics, emphasizing honesty rules, focus on key papers, pre-specified checks, one task per session, human approval of decisions, and transparent AI usage. Applied to two complex problems, it achieved results in days that normally take months, while cautioning against cognitive offloading.
AI.motivation: Analytical theory in soft matter and multiphysics is time-intensive, often requiring months to a year for advanced analyses. The authors aim to leverage AI to accelerate theoretical derivations while maintaining rigor, transparency, and human oversight, and to explore how AI tools can be integrated into graduate education.
AI.method: The proposed framework comprises: (i) setting "honesty rules"; (ii) focusing on a few key papers to formulate the problem; (iii) specifying checks a priori; (iv) using only one task per session with a running log of tasks, checks, corrections, and sessions to prevent error propagation; and (v) ensuring all decisions are approved by humans while AI focuses on execution. This framework was applied to two distinct problems.
AI.result: The framework was applied to (i) diffusiophoresis of a spherical particle with an arbitrary number of electrolytes at arbitrary Debye lengths, and (ii) analytical description of I-V curves, including overlimiting current, in bipolar membranes without water dissociation kinetics. Both advanced analyses, typically requiring months to a year, were solved within a few days.
AI.conclusion: AI-assisted analytical theory can dramatically accelerate research, but increased efficiency must be cautiously navigated to avoid cognitive offloading, ensuring results yield human-readable insights rather than just new formulas. AI usage is presented transparently, and brief thoughts on integrating AI tools into graduate theoretical research education are shared.

title: Amorphous insulating MoS$_x$ films deposited by magnetron sputtering as a low-index optical coating
summary: While much effort are now concentrated on exploration of crystalline form of MoS$_2$ as a two-dimensional material, we show that room-temperature DC magnetron sputtering from pressurized MoS$_2$ powder target produces amorphous MoS$_x$ films with optical properties fundamentally different from those of crystalline MoS$_2$. The films were found to have a sulfur content of approximately $x=1.8$, indicating sulfur deficiency. They are optically isotropic and exhibit rather low optical losses, with a refractive index of about 2 over the visible and near-infrared spectral range. Their compatibility with lift-off lithography and dry etching makes amorphous MoS$_x$ a promising material for integrated photonic applications.

AI.tldr: Room-temperature DC magnetron sputtering of pressurized MoS₂ powder yields amorphous, sulfur-deficient MoSₓ (x≈1.8) films that are optically isotropic, low-loss (n≈2 across visible–NIR), and compatible with lift-off lithography and dry etching, making them promising for integrated photonics.
AI.motivation: Research on MoS₂ as a 2D material has largely focused on its crystalline form, leaving the amorphous phase underexplored. The authors aim to show that amorphous MoSₓ can be produced straightforwardly and possesses optical properties fundamentally distinct from crystalline MoS₂, opening an alternative materials avenue.
AI.method: Amorphous MoSₓ films were deposited at room temperature by DC magnetron sputtering from a pressurized MoS₂ powder target. Film composition was determined (sulfur content x≈1.8), and optical properties (isotropy, refractive index, optical losses) were characterized over the visible and near-infrared range. Process compatibility was assessed via lift-off lithography and dry etching.
AI.result: The films are sulfur-deficient (x≈1.8), optically isotropic, and exhibit relatively low optical losses with a refractive index of about 2 across the visible and near-infrared spectral range. They are compatible with lift-off lithography and dry etching.
AI.conclusion: Amorphous MoSₓ deposited by room-temperature DC magnetron sputtering from a MoS₂ powder target is a promising material for integrated photonic applications, owing to its isotropic, low-loss optical response and CMOS-compatible patterning.

authors: Luiz Henrique Marra da Silva Ribeiro
title: A State-Space Framework for trivial and Topological Metamaterial Stochastic Analysis
summary: Topological phononic crystals and elastic metamaterials support edge states defined by global topological invariants, offering a route toward vibration-control and wave-guiding devices that remain functional in the presence of defects. However, manufacturing-induced spatial variability can perturb these invariants and compromise their robustness, making its quantification essential during design. In this work, we first demonstrate that a previously proposed linear time-varying (LTV) formulation is mathematically equivalent to the spectral element method based on transfer matrices for elementary rod, Saint-Venant shaft, and Euler-Bernoulli beam theories. The deterministic formulation is then extended to stochastic analyses through a stochastic linear time-varying (SLTV) framework. The proposed methodology combines Monte Carlo simulations with stochastic Fourier series and an analytical Karhunen--Loève expansion, providing closed-form stochastic fields and their derivatives required by the LTV formulation. The SLTV approach enables the computation of stochastic dispersion diagrams and forced responses of one-dimensional waveguides with arbitrarily varying geometry and mechanical properties. Because the LTV-based transition matrix isolates individual wavemodes without requiring the mode tracking needed by conventional eigenproblem-based formulations, the framework is particularly suited for evaluating topological invariants, specifically the Zak phase, and assessing the robustness of topological bands under spatial variability. Numerical results for rods, shafts, and Euler-Bernoulli beams demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework as a unified methodology for deterministic and stochastic analyses of trivial and topological periodic waveguides under continuous spatial uncertainty.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes the equivalence between a linear time-varying (LTV) formulation and the spectral element method for rods, shafts, and Euler-Bernoulli beams, then extends it into a stochastic LTV (SLTV) framework combining Monte Carlo, stochastic Fourier series, and Karhunen-Loève expansion to compute stochastic dispersion and forced responses, enabling robust evaluation of topological invariants like the Zak phase under spatial variability.
AI.motivation: Topological phononic crystals and elastic metamaterials offer defect-robust edge states for vibration control, but manufacturing-induced spatial variability can perturb topological invariants and degrade robustness. Quantifying this effect is essential during design, yet existing deterministic formulations typically require mode tracking and lack a unified stochastic treatment.
AI.method: First, the authors prove the mathematical equivalence between a previously proposed LTV formulation and the transfer-matrix-based spectral element method for elementary rod, Saint-Venant shaft, and Euler-Bernoulli beam theories. They then extend the deterministic model to a stochastic linear time-varying (SLTV) framework, integrating Monte Carlo simulations with stochastic Fourier series and an analytical Karhunen-Loève expansion to yield closed-form stochastic fields and their derivatives needed by the LTV formulation.
AI.result: The SLTV approach computes stochastic dispersion diagrams and forced responses of one-dimensional waveguides with arbitrarily varying geometry and mechanical properties. Because the LTV-based transition matrix isolates individual wavemodes without mode tracking, the framework efficiently evaluates topological invariants, specifically the Zak phase, and assesses the robustness of topological bands under spatial variability. Numerical results for rods, shafts, and Euler-Bernoulli beams confirm its applicability.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a unified methodology for deterministic and stochastic analyses of trivial and topological periodic waveguides under continuous spatial uncertainty, offering a practical tool for quantifying the robustness of topological edge states in vibration-control and wave-guiding device design.

title: Interface engineering of spin triplet Cooper pairs for spin-valve implementation
summary: Spin singlet Cooper pairs can be converted into equal-spin triplet pairs at a superconductor/heavy-metal interface under suitable conditions. Under current carrying conditions, these triplet correlations can give rise to a non equilibrium spin moment in the heavy metal through the predicted supercurrent spin-Hall effect. Here we demonstrate that this current induced triplet spin moment, in conjunction with the magnetic moment of a ferromagnetic layer, can enable a magnetic spin-valve response in Nb/Pt/Ni/Pt/Nb vertical nano-devices. The magnitude of this spin-valve effect depends on the efficiency of singlet-triplet Cooper pair conversion at the Nb/Pt interface. In order to facilitate efficient triplet generation, we deliberately introduced interfacial roughness to introduce finite Rashba spin-orbit coupling at the Nb/Pt interface and an out-of-plane component of magnetic moment at the Ni interface. In contrast, no discernible spin-valve response was observed in devices with smooth interfaces within measurement resolutions. Since the magnetic moment of the Ni layer and the current-induced triplet spin moment in the Pt layer are independently switchable using a magnetic field and bias current, respectively, the spin valve can be controlled via either parameters. These results demonstrates a novel approach to directly utilizing the spin polarized triplet Copper pairs in superconducting spintronic applications.

AI.tldr: Interfacial roughness in Nb/Pt/Ni/Pt/Nb vertical spin valves enables Rashba spin-orbit coupling and out-of-plane Ni magnetization, allowing current-induced triplet spin moments in Pt to produce a controllable spin-valve response via either magnetic field or bias current.
AI.motivation: Spin singlet Cooper pairs can convert into equal-spin triplet pairs at a superconductor/heavy-metal interface, and under current-carrying conditions these triplet correlations can generate a non-equilibrium spin moment in the heavy metal via the predicted supercurrent spin-Hall effect. The work aims to exploit this current-induced triplet spin moment together with a ferromagnetic layer's magnetic moment to realize and control a magnetic spin-valve response, thereby directly utilizing spin-polarized triplet Cooper pairs in superconducting spintronics.
AI.method: Nb/Pt/Ni/Pt/Nb vertical nano-devices were fabricated as magnetic spin valves. Interfacial roughness was deliberately introduced to generate finite Rashba spin-orbit coupling at the Nb/Pt interface and an out-of-plane magnetic moment component at the Ni interface, promoting efficient singlet-triplet Cooper pair conversion. Devices with smooth interfaces were measured as controls. The spin-valve response was probed, with the Ni magnetic moment switched by magnetic field and the current-induced triplet spin moment in Pt switched by bias current.
AI.result: The current-induced triplet spin moment, combined with the Ni magnetic moment, enabled a magnetic spin-valve response whose magnitude depends on the efficiency of singlet-triplet Cooper pair conversion at the Nb/Pt interface. Devices with deliberately roughened interfaces showed a discernible spin-valve effect, whereas devices with smooth interfaces exhibited no discernible spin-valve response within measurement resolution. Because the Ni moment and the Pt triplet spin moment are independently switchable by magnetic field and bias current respectively, the spin valve could be controlled through either parameter.
AI.conclusion: Interfacial engineering that induces Rashba spin-orbit coupling and out-of-plane magnetization enables a current-tunable spin-valve effect based on current-induced triplet spin moments in a heavy metal. This demonstrates a novel approach to directly utilizing spin-polarized triplet Cooper pairs in superconducting spintronic applications.

title: Universal Generalized Brillouin Zone Theory I: Review of the Spectral Approach
summary: This series of papers aims to establish a universal generalized Brillouin zone (GBZ) theory for higher-dimensional non-Hermitian systems. As the starting point of this series, we emphasize a fundamental question: while the conventional one-dimensional (1D) GBZ condition, $|β_p| = |β_{p+1}|$, is well known to fail in two dimensions, how does this breakdown actually occur as a system gradually crosses over from 1D to 2D? Investigating this question reveals that the existing 1D GBZ theory itself remains incomplete. In this first paper, we therefore systematically review the 1D spectral approach and clarify where the underlying difficulties lie. Our work identifies the key challenges that motivate the wavefunction approach developed in Paper~II.

AI.tldr: This paper (Paper I of a series) reviews the 1D spectral approach to generalized Brillouin zone theory, argues that the existing 1D GBZ theory is incomplete, and identifies the difficulties that motivate the wavefunction approach of Paper II.
AI.motivation: The series aims to establish a universal GBZ theory for higher-dimensional non-Hermitian systems. The well-known 1D GBZ condition |β_p| = |β_{p+1}| fails in 2D, but how this breakdown emerges as a system crosses over from 1D to 2D is unclear—and probing this question exposes incompleteness in the existing 1D GBZ theory itself.
AI.method: A systematic review of the 1D spectral approach to GBZ theory, analyzing the crossover from 1D to 2D and clarifying where the underlying difficulties lie.
AI.result: The work pinpoints the key challenges of the 1D spectral approach.
AI.conclusion: These identified challenges motivate the wavefunction approach developed in Paper II. This first paper serves as the starting point of the series toward a universal higher-dimensional GBZ theory.

title: Exact Nonperturbative Equilibrium Mode Statistics in Nonlinear Wave and Lattice Systems
summary: We derive exact finite-size nonperturbative representations of equilibrium modal occupations and related statistics for three representative nonlinear systems: the Majda-McLaughlin-Tabak dispersive-wave model, the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou beta anharmonic chain, and the discrete nonlinear Schrodinger lattice field. Independent simulations confirm the predictions from weak to strong nonlinearity. For DNLS, the theory remains accurate across the weak-coupling quasicondensation crossover, where large low-mode occupations and long-range coherence amplify interaction effects even when the bare nonlinear coefficient is small. The finite-ring DNLS occupations are further resolved into a positive sum of Rayleigh-Jeans channels with distinct correlation lengths, explaining when a single Rayleigh-Jeans law applies and why it fails near quasicondensation. In MMT and DNLS, the exact occupations also determine the mean modal frequencies even when the dynamical spectra broaden or split. The nonperturbative results allow a direct assessment of two representative perturbative approaches.
