Treating the mean interaction appropriately yields accurate low-order approximations, including at strong nonlinearity. At higher orders, however, the corrections cease to decrease and successive approximations oscillate with increasing amplitude; both finite-order approaches also fail near weak-coupling quasicondensation. Thus neither low-order agreement nor a small bare coupling guarantees a reliable perturbative description. The results establish nonperturbative equilibrium theory for widely used nonlinear wave and lattice models and provide a quantitative basis for modal distributions of energy, particles, and optical power in nonlinear optics, dispersive waves, anharmonic lattices, and cold-atom systems.

AI.tldr: The paper derives exact finite-size nonperturbative representations of equilibrium modal occupations for three nonlinear systems (MMT, FPU-beta, DNLS), validates them against simulations across weak to strong nonlinearity, and shows that perturbative approaches fail at higher orders and near weak-coupling quasicondensation.
AI.motivation: Equilibrium modal statistics in nonlinear wave and lattice models are widely treated perturbatively, but it is unclear when such expansions are reliable. The authors aim to establish a nonperturbative baseline for modal occupations and related statistics.
AI.method: They derive exact finite-size nonperturbative representations of equilibrium modal occupations and related statistics for three representative nonlinear systems: the Majda-McLaughlin-Tabak dispersive-wave model, the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou beta anharmonic chain, and the discrete nonlinear Schrodinger lattice field. The finite-ring DNLS occupations are resolved into a positive sum of Rayleigh-Jeans channels with distinct correlation lengths. The results are compared with independent simulations and used to assess two perturbative approaches.
AI.result: Independent simulations confirm the theoretical predictions from weak to strong nonlinearity. For DNLS, the theory remains accurate across the weak-coupling quasicondensation crossover, where large low-mode occupations and long-range coherence amplify interaction effects even for small bare nonlinearity. The Rayleigh-Jeans decomposition explains when a single Rayleigh-Jeans law applies and why it fails near quasicondensation. In MMT and DNLS, exact occupations also determine mean modal frequencies even when dynamical spectra broaden or split. Treating the mean interaction appropriately yields accurate low-order perturbative approximations, including at strong nonlinearity; however, at higher orders corrections cease to decrease and successive approximations oscillate with increasing amplitude, and both finite-order approaches fail near weak-coupling quasicondensation.
AI.conclusion: Nonperturbative equilibrium theory is established for widely used nonlinear wave and lattice models, providing a quantitative basis for modal distributions of energy, particles, and optical power in nonlinear optics, dispersive waves, anharmonic lattices, and cold-atom systems. Neither low-order agreement nor a small bare coupling guarantees a reliable perturbative description.

title: Decoupling the Magnetic Field Operator as an Independent Operator Class in Stochastic Series Expansion Quantum Monte Carlo
summary: The Stochastic Series Expansion (SSE) quantum Monte Carlo method with loop updates is among the most powerful approaches for quantum spin and boson systems. In the standard formulation, the magnetic field term is routinely absorbed into the Heisenberg interactions---a strategy that has proven highly efficient across a wide range of field strengths. In this work, we propose a more general SSE framework in which the magnetic field operator is treated as an independent operator class, enabling it to participate in Monte Carlo updates on an equal footing with all other operators. Importantly, the field operator and other interaction operators can transform into one another during the update process. We demonstrate this algorithm using the two-dimensional antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model in a magnetic field as a concrete example. The simulation results agree with those of the conventional algorithm, confirming the correctness of the new formulation. A comparison of the integrated autocorrelation time shows that the new algorithm is competitive. This flexibility not only facilitates measurements of observables associated with operators but also offers potential computational advantages for a broader class of problems.

AI.tldr: A generalized Stochastic Series Expansion (SSE) quantum Monte Carlo framework is proposed in which the magnetic field operator is treated as an independent operator class that participates in loop updates on equal footing with interaction operators, with operators able to interconvert during updates; validated on the 2D antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model in a field, showing correctness and competitive autocorrelation times.
AI.motivation: In the standard SSE formulation with loop updates, the magnetic field term is customarily absorbed into the Heisenberg interactions, a strategy that is efficient across a wide range of field strengths but restricts the field operator's role in the update process and limits flexibility for measuring operator-related observables.
AI.method: The authors develop a more general SSE framework in which the magnetic field operator is defined as an independent operator class, allowing it to take part in Monte Carlo updates on an equal footing with all other operators. Crucially, the field operator and other interaction operators can transform into one another during the update process. The algorithm is demonstrated using the two-dimensional antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model in a magnetic field.
AI.result: Simulation results agree with those of the conventional algorithm, confirming the correctness of the new formulation. A comparison of the integrated autocorrelation time indicates that the new algorithm is competitive.
AI.conclusion: Treating the magnetic field operator as an independent class in SSE provides flexibility that facilitates measurements of observables associated with operators and offers potential computational advantages for a broader class of problems.

title: Revealing epitaxial relationships at Ga$_2$O$_3$ interfaces with p-type oxides
summary: p-type oxide contact layers such as Cr$_2$O$_3$ and NiO are attracting increasing interest in pn-heterojunctions with n-type monoclinic $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ for high-power electronic devices and other extreme environment applications. However, scientific understanding of their epitaxial relationships remains incomplete. In this work we investigate the epitaxial relation of Cr$_2$O$_3$ and NiO layers to (001) and ($\bar{2}$01) out-of-plane oriented Ga$_2$O$_3$ substrates. Surprisingly, we find that, for the most commercially relevant (001)-orientation of the Ga$_2$O$_3$ substrate, the epitaxial relationships are Cr$_2$O$_3$ (0001) and NiO (111) $\parallel$ Ga$_2$O$_3$ (101), both at the non-intuitive $χ$ = 22.5 $^\circ$ angle with respect to the substrate normal. We explain this unusual discovery by the interfacial atomistic bonding dominated by oxygen sublattice equivalence of these Cr$_2$O$_3$ and NiO polar surface orientations to the tilted Ga$_2$O$_3$ (101), rather than Ga$_2$O$_3$ (001) substrate surface planes. Furthermore, we assign the in-plane orientation for Cr$_2$O$_3$ on ($\bar{2}$01)-oriented Ga$_2$O$_3$ as: Cr$_2$O$_3$ $[12\bar{3}0]$ $\parallel$ Ga$_2$O$_3$ $[010]$ with two in-plane rotational domains. Interface modeling confirms the in-plane orientation for Cr$_2$O$_3$/$(\bar{2}01)$ Ga$_2$O$_3$ and shows that strained O-terminated Ga$_2$O$_3$ $(\bar{2}01)$ surfaces have the lowest interfacial energy with Cr$_2$O$_3$ (0001). Beyond establishing the specific epitaxial relationships for Cr$_2$O$_3$ and NiO on Ga$_2$O$_3$, this work provides a systematic methodology for the unambiguous structural characterization of heterointerfaces involving materials with markedly different crystal symmetries.

AI.tldr: This work establishes the epitaxial relationships of p-type Cr2O3 and NiO on β-Ga2O3 substrates, revealing an unexpected bonding-driven alignment at a 22.5° tilt for (001) Ga2O3 and providing a systematic methodology for heterointerface characterization.
AI.motivation: p-type oxide contact layers like Cr2O3 and NiO on n-type β-Ga2O3 are promising for high-power and extreme-environment devices, but the epitaxial relationships governing these pn-heterojunctions remain poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors investigated the epitaxial relation of Cr2O3 and NiO layers grown on (001) and (-201) out-of-plane oriented β-Ga2O3 substrates, using structural characterization and interface modeling to determine out-of-plane and in-plane orientations and interfacial energies.
AI.result: For (001) Ga2O3, Cr2O3 (0001) and NiO (111) align parallel to Ga2O3 (101) at a non-intuitive χ = 22.5° to the substrate normal, driven by oxygen sublattice equivalence. For (-201) Ga2O3, Cr2O3 [12-30] ∥ Ga2O3 [010] with two in-plane rotational domains; modeling shows strained O-terminated Ga2O3 (-201) surfaces have the lowest interfacial energy with Cr2O3 (0001).
AI.conclusion: The study clarifies specific epitaxial relationships of Cr2O3 and NiO on Ga2O3, explains unusual alignments via interfacial oxygen sublattice bonding, and offers a systematic methodology for unambiguous structural characterization of heterointerfaces between materials of markedly different crystal symmetries.

title: From Heuristics to Machine Learning: The Performance Ceiling for Single-Ion Magnets and Its Electronic Origin
comment: 41 pages including Supporting Information, 9 figures in the main text
summary: Machine learning (ML) is expected to speed up the discovery of single-ion magnets (SIMs), but does the structural information available before synthesis allow such predictions? For 1215 lanthanide complexes from the SIMDAVIS 1.2.1 database we compared three increasing levels of structural description: tabular features of the coordination site, continuous symmetry measures of the coordination polyhedron, and the complete 3D arrangement of atoms. All three converge to an accuracy near 76%, only slightly above the 71% of the single rule "predict SIM for Dy3+". To explain the failures, we combined multireference ab initio calculations with an inspection of the structures behind the high-confidence errors. The SIMs missed by the geometric models are field-induced relaxers whose ground Kramers doublets are prone to tunnelling, a property invisible to geometric descriptors. Many false positives contain several lanthanide centers or radicals, so their relaxation is collective and outside the single-ion picture. The electronic-structure and connectivity information needed to identify SIMs is therefore not accessible to geometric methods alone. Geometric models remain useful: restricting the screening to compounds with high prediction confidence raises the accuracy to 88% while retaining 48% of the dataset. Building on the analysis of the failures, we propose a strategy that combines simple filters for nuclearity and for radicals with ligand-field descriptors from ab initio calculations.

AI.tldr: Geometric ML models predict single-ion magnets at only ~76% accuracy, barely above the trivial Dy3+ rule (71%), because tunnelling and collective relaxation are invisible to geometric descriptors; adding ab initio ligand-field data with filters for nuclearity and radicals is proposed.
AI.motivation: ML is expected to accelerate the discovery of single-ion magnets (SIMs), but it is unclear whether structural information available prior to synthesis suffices for such predictions. The paper tests the limits of purely geometric descriptions.
AI.method: Using 1215 lanthanide complexes from the SIMDAVIS 1.2.1 database, three increasing levels of structural description were compared: tabular features of the coordination site, continuous symmetry measures of the coordination polyhedron, and the complete 3D atomic arrangement. Failures were then investigated by combining multireference ab initio calculations with inspection of structures behind high-confidence errors.
AI.result: All three geometric representations converge to ~76% accuracy, only slightly above the 71% baseline of the single rule "predict SIM for Dy3+". Missed SIMs are field-induced relaxers whose ground Kramers doublets are prone to tunnelling, a property invisible to geometric descriptors; many false positives contain several lanthanide centers or radicals, giving collective rather than single-ion relaxation. Restricting screening to high-confidence predictions raises accuracy to 88% while retaining 48% of the dataset.
AI.conclusion: Electronic-structure and connectivity information required to identify SIMs is not accessible to geometric methods alone. Nonetheless, geometric models remain useful for confidence-based screening, and the authors propose combining simple nuclearity and radical filters with ligand-field descriptors from ab initio calculations.

title: Random-matrix and transport frequencies in eigenstate spectral functions
summary: The fact that generic isolated many-body quantum systems thermalize is understood using the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH). In recent years, there has been much interest in the behavior of the ETH spectral functions, which characterize the smooth dependence of the variance of the off-diagonal matrix elements of observables on the associated energy and frequency, and whose low-frequency part contains information about the long-time dynamics. In finite systems described by the ETH, the spectral functions are expected to exhibit plateaus below a characteristic frequency $ω^{}_{\mathrm{ETH}}$. In this regime, the statistics of the matrix elements of observables are expected to be described by random matrix theory. Related frequencies that have been studied in the literature are $ω^{}_{\mathrm{SFF}}$, which controls the onset of random-matrix behavior in the spectral form factor, and the transport frequencies $ω^{}_{\mathrm{tr}}$, which are derived from transport coefficients. However, a direct quantitative comparison of these frequencies is lacking. Using exact diagonalization, we conduct such a comparison for the spectral functions of current operators in clean and disordered quantum spin ladders with diffusive energy and spin transport. We find clear evidence for the expected low-frequency plateaus in the ETH spectral functions. For the accessible system sizes, $ω^{}_{\mathrm{SFF}}$ is consistent with the extent of the plateaus, while the transport frequencies are systematically larger and lie in the nonuniversal regime of the spectral functions. Our findings highlight the need to better understand the origin of these quantitative differences.

AI.tldr: The paper numerically compares three characteristic frequency scales in the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) spectral functions using exact diagonalization of clean and disordered quantum spin ladders with diffusive transport.
AI.motivation: The ETH spectral functions characterize the smooth dependence of the variance of off-diagonal matrix elements on energy and frequency, with their low-frequency part encoding long-time dynamics. Several related frequency scales—ω_ETH (onset of the plateau), ω_SFF (onset of random-matrix behavior in the spectral form factor), and transport frequencies ω_tr (from transport coefficients)—have been studied separately, but a direct quantitative comparison among them has been lacking.
AI.method: Exact diagonalization is used to compute the ETH spectral functions of current operators in clean and disordered quantum spin ladders that exhibit diffusive energy and spin transport. The authors then compare the extent of the low-frequency plateaus with ω_SFF and ω_tr.
AI.result: Clear evidence is found for the expected low-frequency plateaus in the ETH spectral functions. For the accessible system sizes, ω_SFF is consistent with the extent of the plateaus, whereas the transport frequencies are systematically larger and lie in the nonuniversal regime of the spectral functions.
AI.conclusion: The quantitative mismatch between ω_SFF (plateau extent) and ω_tr (transport frequencies) highlights the need to better understand the origin of these differences among ETH-related frequency scales.

title: LiNiO2/NiO Phase Prediction Using Artificial Neural Networks
summary: In the realm of material analysis, identifying different material phases is of key importance. Artificial intelligence in the form of neural networks provides a very fast and, once trained, computationally inexpensive method for analysing large amounts of image data, like the sets of diffraction patterns generated during four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) dataset acquisition. In this work, we train multiple network architectures on images of this type to distinguish between the phases of LiNiO2 and NiO, an important and challenging distinction in the lithium-ion battery community, since the formation of NiO limits battery capacity. We test both classical convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and different forms of vision transformers (ViTs). Our networks are trained on synthetic images and tested on experimentally recorded diffraction patterns. Additionally, we also investigate the decision-making of our networks using the GradCAM method. We test our networks on both synthetic as well as experimental diffraction patterns. Our networks exhibit very robust results, especially when dealing with highly varying data, an area where traditional template-matching methods typically struggle.

AI.tldr: Neural networks (CNNs and ViTs) trained on synthetic 4DSTEM diffraction patterns distinguish LiNiO2 from NiO phases, generalizing well to experimental data and outperforming template matching under high variability.
AI.motivation: Identifying distinct material phases is crucial in material analysis, and the LiNiO2/NiO distinction is particularly important for lithium-ion batteries since NiO formation reduces capacity. 4DSTEM generates massive image datasets, motivating fast, low-cost automated analysis via neural networks.
AI.method: Multiple network architectures—classical CNNs and several variants of vision transformers (ViTs)—were trained on synthetic diffraction patterns and tested on both synthetic and experimentally recorded patterns. GradCAM was applied to interpret network decision-making.
AI.result: The networks achieved robust phase discrimination, especially on highly varying data where conventional template-matching approaches typically fail, and generalized from synthetic training data to experimental diffraction patterns.
AI.conclusion: Neural-network-based phase classification, including both CNNs and ViTs, offers a fast and reliable alternative to template matching for 4DSTEM phase identification, with interpretability supported by GradCAM.

title: Experiments and Modeling of Defect Dynamics and BTI Behavior in Doped InO TFTs during $400^\circ$C Post-Processing Forming Gas Annealing
summary: We investigate the impact of a monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) integration process-critical $400^\circ$C post-processing forming gas anneal (FGA) on the electrical performance, reliability, and defect evolution of oxide-channel thin-film transistors (TFTs), combining systematic experiments with density-functional-theory (DFT)-based liquid-quench molecular-dynamics (MD) simulations. Indium tungsten oxide (IWO) TFTs are employed as a model system and encapsulated with a thin 3 nm Al$_2$O$_3$ / 3 nm HfO$_2$ hybrid layer that effectively suppresses external hydrogen ingress. We reveal a non-monotonic evolution of device behavior during FGA, governed by initial densification followed by partial crystallization. Short-duration FGA (10 min) induces channel densification and the formation of shallow, delocalized defect states, leading to pronounced positive bias temperature instability (PBTI) degradation and the emergence of a characteristic transfer-curve "kink." With prolonged annealing (>40 min), partial crystallization of the oxide channel occurs, stabilizing hydrogen in deep, localized defect states, suppressing hydrogen mobility, and restoring device reliability. As a result, the PBTI shift is reduced to 10.4 mV after 2000 seconds of stress, accompanied by complete elimination of the transfer-curve kink. These findings provide a mechanistic understanding of hydrogen-defect interactions during high-temperature post-processing FGA and demonstrate that appropriate hydrogen-blocking encapsulation enables oxide-channel TFT integration without compromising electrical performance or reliability.

AI.tldr: A $400^\circ$C forming gas anneal in oxide-channel (IWO) TFTs causes non-monotonic reliability behavior: short anneals degrade PBTI and create a transfer-curve kink, while prolonged annealing (>40 min) partially crystallizes the channel, stabilizes hydrogen in deep defect states, and restores reliability (PBTI shift 10.4 mV at 2000 s).
AI.motivation: Monolithic 3D (M3D) integration requires low-thermal-budget, process-critical steps such as a $400^\circ$C post-processing forming gas anneal (FGA), but the impact of this hydrogen-rich anneal on oxide-channel TFT electrical performance, reliability, and defect evolution is not well understood. A mechanistic picture of hydrogen-defect interactions under such processing is needed to enable M3D integration without sacrificing device quality.
AI.method: The study combines systematic experiments with density-functional-theory (DFT)-based liquid-quench molecular-dynamics (MD) simulations. Indium tungsten oxide (IWO) TFTs serve as the model system, encapsulated with a thin 3 nm Al$_2$O$_3$ / 3 nm HfO$_2$ hybrid layer to suppress external hydrogen ingress. Annealing time is varied to track device behavior, defect states, and PBTI response.
AI.result: Device behavior evolves non-monotonically during FGA. Short-duration FGA (10 min) causes channel densification and shallow, delocalized defect states, producing pronounced PBTI degradation and a characteristic transfer-curve "kink." Prolonged annealing (>40 min) leads to partial channel crystallization that stabilizes hydrogen in deep, localized defect states and suppresses hydrogen mobility, restoring reliability. The PBTI shift drops to 10.4 mV after 2000 s of stress, with the transfer-curve kink fully eliminated.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a mechanistic understanding of hydrogen-defect interactions during high-temperature post-processing FGA, showing that the competing effects of densification and partial crystallization govern defect depth and hydrogen mobility. It demonstrates that appropriate hydrogen-blocking encapsulation allows oxide-channel TFT integration without compromising electrical performance or reliability.

title: Generalized conditions for odd-frequency pairing in superconducting systems
summary: Odd-frequency superconducting pairing has been predicted to arise in many systems and is known to lead to phenomena such as paramagnetic Meissner response and long-range superconducting proximity effect. Here, we provide generalized necessary and sufficient conditions for odd-frequency pairing appearing in any superconducting system, from bulk superconductors to superconducting hybrid structures. This generalizes an earlier first-order expression in multiband bulk superconductors to all superconducting systems and to all orders, in both order parameter and frequency. We then apply the derived conditions to several systems, including superconducting-ferromagnet and superconducting Josephson junctions, as well as a transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer proximitized by a conventional superconductor, where the generalized conditions are used to understand the properties of the superconducting state.

AI.tldr: The paper derives generalized necessary and sufficient conditions for odd-frequency superconducting pairing valid in any superconducting system and to all orders in both order parameter and frequency, then applies them to hybrid structures and a proximitized transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer.
AI.motivation: Odd-frequency pairing is predicted to cause notable effects like paramagnetic Meissner response and long-range proximity effect, but existing conditions were limited to a first-order expression in multiband bulk superconductors. A general framework covering all superconducting systems and all orders was needed.
AI.method: The authors generalize the earlier first-order condition for odd-frequency pairing to all superconducting systems (bulk and hybrid) and to all orders in order parameter and frequency, deriving necessary and sufficient conditions, then apply these to superconducting-ferromagnet junctions, superconducting Josephson junctions, and a transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer proximitized by a conventional superconductor.
AI.result: The generalized conditions successfully describe and clarify the properties of the superconducting state in the studied systems, including superconducting-ferromagnet and Josephson junctions and the proximitized transition metal dichalcogenide monolayer.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a universal set of necessary and sufficient conditions for odd-frequency pairing applicable across all superconducting systems and orders, offering a general tool for understanding superconducting states in hybrid and proximitized structures.

title: Multiscale Modeling of Ion Transport in Nanopores: Fitting Implicit-Water Radial Diffusion Profiles to Explicit-Water Molecular Dynamics
summary: We develop a multiscale approach for incorporating molecular-scale transport information into computationally efficient models of ion transport through nanopores. A radially varying effective diffusion coefficient profile is fitted to radial conductivity profiles obtained from explicit-water molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The fitting is performed within the NP+LEMC framework, which combines the Nernst--Planck equation with Local Equilibrium Monte Carlo to account for ion correlations beyond mean-field approximation. We apply the approach to NaCl, CaCl$_2$, and their mixtures in a negatively charged silica nanopore. The resulting diffusion coefficient profiles reproduce the radial current distributions of the MD simulations, including the strong suppression of ionic mobility near the pore wall that cannot be captured by a spatially constant diffusion coefficient inside the pore. NaCl and CaCl$_2$ exhibit qualitatively different transport behavior: the former is cation selective due to enhanced near-wall Na$^+$ conduction, whereas the latter shows weak anion selectivity because strongly bound Ca$^{2+}$ ions have strongly suppressed mobility near the surface. For NaCl--CaCl$_2$ mixtures, preferential Ca$^{2+}$ binding leads to nonlinear changes in ionic conductance. The approach establishes a bridge between experimentally relevant device behavior and computationally efficient reduced models, with explicit-water MD providing the molecular-scale information that can be incorporated into the effective transport coefficients.

AI.tldr: A multiscale method fits radially varying effective diffusion-coefficient profiles (derived from explicit-water MD radial conductivity) into the NP+LEMC framework, reproducing MD radial ion currents in a charged silica nanopore and revealing distinct NaCl/CaCl2 selectivity and mixture effects.
AI.motivation: Computationally efficient continuum models of ion transport through nanopores cannot capture molecular-scale effects such as strong mobility suppression near pore walls when a spatially constant diffusion coefficient is used. A bridge is needed between experimentally relevant device behavior and efficient reduced models, with explicit-water MD supplying the missing molecular-scale transport information.
AI.method: A multiscale approach is developed: a radially varying effective diffusion coefficient profile is fitted to radial conductivity profiles obtained from explicit-water MD simulations. The fitting is performed within the NP+LEMC framework, which couples the Nernst-Planck equation with Local Equilibrium Monte Carlo to capture ion correlations beyond the mean-field approximation. The approach is applied to NaCl, CaCl2, and their mixtures in a negatively charged silica nanopore.
AI.result: The resulting diffusion coefficient profiles reproduce the radial current distributions of the MD simulations, including the strong suppression of ionic mobility near the pore wall that a spatially constant diffusion coefficient cannot capture. NaCl and CaCl2 show qualitatively different transport: NaCl is cation selective due to enhanced near-wall Na+ conduction, whereas CaCl2 shows weak anion selectivity because strongly bound Ca2+ ions have strongly suppressed near-surface mobility. In NaCl-CaCl2 mixtures, preferential Ca2+ binding produces nonlinear changes in ionic conductance.
AI.conclusion: The approach establishes a bridge between experimentally relevant device behavior and computationally efficient reduced models, with explicit-water MD providing the molecular-scale information incorporated into effective transport coefficients.

title: Derivation of the Thiele equation for magnetic skyrmions using the Mori-Zwanzig formalism
summary: We use the Mori-Zwanzig formalism to derive an exact generalized Langevin equation governing the dynamics of magnetic skyrmions. Using standard approximations, this generalized Langevin equation is found to reduce to the usual Thiele equation. Our approach provides a general route for obtaining extensions of the Thiele equation applicable to magnetic textures and degrees of freedom not covered by the standard derivation route. It also provides some insights into the microscopic justification of the standard Thiele equation, specifically concerning contributions of fast modes to the form of the drift and diffusion terms in the Fokker-Planck equation for skyrmions.

AI.tldr: Using the Mori-Zwanzig formalism, the authors derive an exact generalized Langevin equation for magnetic skyrmion dynamics, which reduces to the standard Thiele equation under standard approximations.
AI.motivation: The standard Thiele equation for skyrmion dynamics lacks a rigorous microscopic justification, and there is no general route to extend it to magnetic textures and degrees of freedom beyond the standard derivation.
AI.method: Application of the Mori-Zwanzig projection formalism to derive an exact generalized Langevin equation, followed by standard approximations to recover the Thiele equation.
AI.result: The exact generalized Langevin equation reduces to the usual Thiele equation under standard approximations, and it clarifies how fast modes contribute to the drift and diffusion terms in the skyrmion Fokker-Planck equation.
AI.conclusion: The approach offers a general route for obtaining extensions of the Thiele equation applicable to magnetic textures and degrees of freedom beyond standard derivations, and provides microscopic insight into the standard Thiele equation.

title: A Majorana Formulation of Time-Dependent Two-Particle Reduced-Density-Matrix Dynamics
summary: We introduce a time-dependent two-particle (TP) reduced-density-matrix algorithm for systems of interacting Majorana fermions. We close the BBGKY hierarchy at the two-particle level by reconstructing the three-particle reduced density matrix from lower-order correlations. To stabilize the evolution, we impose a positivity projection on the two-particle density matrix while preserving chosen conserved quantities such as the energy. We benchmark the approach on quenches in the one-dimensional Hubbard model and on flux dynamics in the Kitaev honeycomb model. For the Hubbard quench, TP captures strong-coupling dynamics missed by Hartree--Fock (HF). For the Kitaev quenches, TP accurately reproduces the early-time flux dynamics in several regimes and provides a substantial improvement over HF when two-particle correlations are important. We further show that gauge coherence is essential for flux dynamics. The projection procedure however introduces an effective irreversibility, which affects the long-time dynamics.

AI.tldr: The authors introduce a time-dependent two-particle reduced-density-matrix (TP-RDM) method for interacting Majorana fermions, closing the BBGKY hierarchy at the two-particle level with a positivity projection that preserves conserved quantities, and benchmark it on Hubbard and Kitaev honeycomb models, showing improved accuracy over Hartree-Fock.
AI.motivation: Simulating nonequilibrium dynamics of strongly correlated fermionic systems is challenging. Mean-field approaches like Hartree-Fock miss strong-coupling and two-particle correlation effects, motivating a systematically improvable, lower-cost method that captures these correlations.
AI.method: A time-dependent two-particle reduced-density-matrix algorithm for interacting Majorana fermions. The BBGKY hierarchy is truncated at the two-particle level by reconstructing the three-particle RDM from lower-order correlations. A positivity projection is applied to the two-particle density matrix while preserving selected conserved quantities such as energy, stabilizing the evolution.
AI.result: Benchmarked on quenches in the 1D Hubbard model and flux dynamics in the Kitaev honeycomb model. For the Hubbard quench, TP captures strong-coupling dynamics missed by Hartree-Fock. For the Kitaev quenches, TP accurately reproduces early-time flux dynamics across several regimes and substantially improves on HF when two-particle correlations matter. Gauge coherence is shown to be essential for flux dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The TP-RDM approach provides an efficient and accurate framework for nonequilibrium dynamics of interacting Majorana fermions beyond mean-field theory, capturing strong-coupling and two-particle correlation effects. However, the positivity projection introduces an effective irreversibility that affects long-time dynamics, limiting the method's validity at later times.

title: Composition-Dependent Self-Diffusion Coefficients in Liquid Mixtures from Hybrid Machine Learning
summary: Self-diffusion coefficients are key descriptors of molecular mobility, yet experimental data remain scarce, highlighting the need for reliable prediction methods. In previous work, we introduced the hybrid Enhanced Stokes-Einstein (ESE) model, which advanced the state of the art in the physically consistent prediction of self-diffusion coefficients of solutes at infinite dilution in pure solvents by integrating the Stokes-Einstein equation with machine learning (ML). Here, we extend this approach to concentration-dependent self-diffusion coefficients and multicomponent solvents with HADES. This hybrid architecture leverages a deep-set neural network to connect pure-component and mixture prediction within a single framework. HADES predicts self-diffusion coefficients in liquid mixtures with any number of components at any composition and temperature. The only required inputs are SMILES-encoded molecular structures of the components and the pure-component viscosities, making the method broadly applicable. Trained and evaluated on a comprehensive dataset of 2526 data points for 600 systems, HADES significantly outperforms benchmark prediction methods. The trained model and its source code are fully disclosed, and the application is available via an interactive website https://ml-prop.mv.rptu.de/.

AI.tldr: HADES extends the hybrid Enhanced Stokes-Einstein (ESE) model to predict concentration-dependent self-diffusion coefficients in multicomponent liquid mixtures.
AI.motivation: Experimental self-diffusion coefficient data are scarce, and prior work (the ESE model) only handled solutes at infinite dilution in pure solvents, leaving concentration-dependent and multicomponent mixture prediction unaddressed.
AI.method: HADES is a hybrid architecture combining the Stokes-Einstein equation with a deep-set neural network that connects pure-component and mixture prediction within a single framework. Inputs are SMILES-encoded molecular structures of components plus pure-component viscosities; it predicts self-diffusion coefficients for any number of components, composition, and temperature.
AI.result: Trained and evaluated on 2526 data points across 600 systems, HADES significantly outperforms benchmark prediction methods.
AI.conclusion: HADES provides a broadly applicable, physically consistent predictor of concentration-dependent self-diffusion coefficients in multicomponent mixtures; the trained model, source code, and an interactive website are fully disclosed.

title: Three-dimensional atom-by-atom measurement of interface diffusion dynamics
summary: Diffusion at interfaces governs how materials and devices form, evolve and function. It is usually measured through smooth concentration profiles and bulk transport coefficients, which average over the discrete atomic rearrangements. At nanoscale interfaces only a few atomic layers wide, however, such coarse-graining obscures the local three-dimensional (3D) atomic transport, and scalar diffusion coefficients cannot fully describe species-, layer- and facet-resolved redistribution. The essential observable is the discrete 3D redistribution of atoms themselves, beyond an averaged profile. Here we combine micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) pulse-quench heating with atomic electron tomography (AET) to reconstruct five 3D atomic configurations of the same coherent Pd@Pt core-shell nanoparticle, each corresponding to a well-defined thermal state. Species-conserving one-to-one assignment links neighbouring configurations, and labelled reference simulations correct the displacement bias caused by indistinguishable same-species atoms. The corrected Pd diffusivities follow Arrhenius behaviour, giving an apparent activation energy of 1.10 eV, consistent with migration-limited vacancy-mediated transport. Atomic-layer transition statistics further show that increasing 3D mobility can coexist with declining net chemical transfer and reveal facet-dependent pathways hidden by the scalar diffusivity. Together, these measurements establish a 3D atom-by-atom framework that connects identity-corrected mobility to species-, layer- and facet-resolved transport at buried nanointerfaces.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a 3D atom-by-atom framework for measuring diffusion at buried nanoscale interfaces by combining MEMS pulse-quench heating with atomic electron tomography on the same Pd@Pt core-shell nanoparticle across five thermal states.
AI.motivation: Conventional diffusion measurements rely on smooth concentration profiles and bulk transport coefficients that average over discrete atomic rearrangements. At nanoscale interfaces only a few atomic layers wide, this coarse-graining obscures local 3D atomic transport, and scalar diffusion coefficients cannot describe species-, layer-, and facet-resolved redistribution. The essential observable is the discrete 3D redistribution of atoms themselves.
AI.method: MEMS pulse-quench heating combined with atomic electron tomography (AET) to reconstruct five 3D atomic configurations of the same coherent Pd@Pt core-shell nanoparticle, each corresponding to a well-defined thermal state. Species-conserving one-to-one assignment links neighbouring configurations, and labelled reference simulations correct the displacement bias caused by indistinguishable same-species atoms.
AI.result: Corrected Pd diffusivities follow Arrhenius behaviour with an apparent activation energy of 1.10 eV, consistent with migration-limited vacancy-mediated transport. Atomic-layer transition statistics show that increasing 3D mobility can coexist with declining net chemical transfer, and reveal facet-dependent pathways hidden by the scalar diffusivity.
AI.conclusion: These measurements establish a 3D atom-by-atom framework that connects identity-corrected mobility to species-, layer-, and facet-resolved transport at buried nanointerfaces.

title: Electronic Reconstruction Towards Topological Superconductivity in FeTe
comment: 35 pages and 4 figures. Comments are very much welcome
summary: The recent discovery of intrinsic superconductivity in stoichiometric FeTe films has renewed interest in the Te-rich end member of the iron chalcogenides for studies of unconventional and topological superconductivity, yet its intrinsic electronic structure remains unresolved. In this work, we combine molecular beam epitaxy, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), electrical transport measurements, density functional theory, and embedded dynamical mean-field theory to track the electronic reconstruction of 20-unit-cell FeTe films as Te annealing progressively removes excess interstitial Fe and drives the system from an antiferromagnetic metal to a superconductor. We find that this evolution is accompanied by recovered quasiparticle coherence, reduced electronic correlations, a Lifshitz transition, and a topological phase transition, yielding dxy-dominated hole and electron pockets that favor inter-pocket scattering. In addition, a shallow dxz/dyz-derived hole band located about 2 meV below the Fermi level may provide an incipient-band pairing channel, while scattering between the two electron pockets at M may offer additional pairing channels. High-resolution polarization-dependent laser ARPES measurements further reveal a topological surface state whose circular dichroism is consistent with the expected orbital-angular-momentum texture of stoichiometric FeTe. These results establish the intrinsic low-energy electronic structure of superconducting FeTe and identify the electronic states most relevant to superconductivity. The coexistence of intrinsic superconductivity and a topological surface state establishes stoichiometric FeTe as a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity and possible Majorana bound states.

AI.tldr: This work resolves the intrinsic low-energy electronic structure of stoichiometric FeTe films, tracking how Te annealing drives an electronic reconstruction from an antiferromagnetic metal to a superconductor that hosts both unconventional pairing states and a topological surface state.
AI.motivation: Intrinsic superconductivity in stoichiometric FeTe films has renewed interest in the Te-rich end member of the iron chalcogenides for unconventional and topological superconductivity studies, but its intrinsic electronic structure had remained unresolved.
AI.method: The authors combine molecular beam epitaxy, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), electrical transport measurements, density functional theory, and embedded dynamical mean-field theory to track the electronic reconstruction of 20-unit-cell FeTe films as Te annealing progressively removes excess interstitial Fe. High-resolution polarization-dependent laser ARPES is used to probe the topological surface state.
AI.result: As excess interstitial Fe is removed, the system evolves from an antiferromagnetic metal to a superconductor, accompanied by recovered quasiparticle coherence, reduced electronic correlations, a Lifshitz transition, and a topological phase transition. This yields dxy-dominated hole and electron pockets favoring inter-pocket scattering. A shallow dxz/dyz-derived hole band about 2 meV below the Fermi level may provide an incipient-band pairing channel, and scattering between the two electron pockets at M may offer additional pairing channels. Laser ARPES reveals a topological surface state whose circular dichroism matches the expected orbital-angular-momentum texture of stoichiometric FeTe.
AI.conclusion: The results establish the intrinsic low-energy electronic structure of superconducting FeTe and identify the electronic states most relevant to superconductivity. The coexistence of intrinsic superconductivity and a topological surface state makes stoichiometric FeTe a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity and possible Majorana bound states.

title: Interplay of spin-orbit coupling and magnetic chirality: Multidirectional spin polarization in a helical antiferromagnet
summary: We investigate spin-dependent transport in a non-collinear helical antiferromagnet in the presence of spin-orbit coupling within a tight-binding framework. Using the Landauer-Büttiker formalism, we analyze the generation of spin polarization arising from the combined effects of the helical magnetic texture and spin-orbit interaction. We find that finite spin polarization can be generated simultaneously along the $\hat{x}$, $\hat{y}$, and $\hat{z}$-directions, in contrast to the predominantly single-axis spin polarization commonly observed in conventional spin-filtering systems. The multidirectional spin polarization originates from the symmetry breaking introduced by the non-collinear magnetic order. We further show that the spin polarization is modified significantly in the presence of spin-orbit coupling and it has strong dependence on the parameters associated with the helical system. In particular, long-range hopping significantly enhances the spin-filtering effect, leading to large spin polarization components along all three spatial directions.

AI.tldr: Spin-dependent transport in a non-collinear helical antiferromagnet with spin-orbit coupling is studied via the Landauer-Büttiker formalism, revealing simultaneous multi-directional spin polarization that is tunable by helical and hopping parameters.
AI.motivation: Conventional spin-filtering systems typically produce spin polarization predominantly along a single axis. The authors aim to explore whether non-collinear magnetic order combined with spin-orbit coupling can break this limitation and generate spin polarization along multiple spatial directions.
AI.method: A tight-binding framework is employed to model a non-collinear helical antiferromagnet with spin-orbit coupling, and the Landauer-Büttiker formalism is used to compute spin-dependent transport and spin polarization along the x, y, and z directions.
AI.result: Finite spin polarization is generated simultaneously along x, y, and z directions, in contrast to the single-axis polarization of conventional spin filters. This multi-directional polarization stems from symmetry breaking induced by the non-collinear magnetic order, is strongly modified by spin-orbit coupling, and depends sensitively on helical system parameters. Long-range hopping significantly enhances the spin-filtering effect, yielding large polarization components in all three spatial directions.
AI.conclusion: Non-collinear helical antiferromagnets with spin-orbit coupling enable multi-directional spin polarization, offering a tunable platform for spin-filtering devices where long-range hopping and helical parameters serve as effective control knobs.

title: Ageing in the exact correlations of the voter model on a fractal
summary: The exact behaviour of the enveloppes of the single-time and two-time correlators is found for the voter model on a fractal substrate, with nearest-neighbour interactions. Herein the geometry of the fractal substrate is described by its non-integer geometric fractal dimension $d_f$, and its topology and diffusive transport by the distinct spectral dimension $d_s$. On the level of the equations of motion of the correlators this can be modelled by considering a space-dependent diffusion constant ${\cal D}(r)\sim r^{-θ}$ which implies the spectral index $θ$, itself a function of $d_f$ and $d_s$. With a scaling ansatz, the generic phenomenology of ageing is confirmed and the dynamic exponent ${z}=2+θ$ and the autocorrelation exponent $λ=d_f$ are derived. The explicitly found dynamic scaling functions are shown to depend only on the spectral dimension $d_s$. The decay of the enveloppe of the density of active interfaces with time is described by the exponent $α=1-d_s/2$ for $d_s<2$, confirming the results of preexisting numerical simulations.

AI.tldr: The exact envelope behaviour of single-time and two-time correlators for the voter model on a fractal substrate (nearest-neighbour interactions) is derived, with geometry given by fractal dimension d_f and transport by spectral dimension d_s. Dynamic exponent z=2+θ, autocorrelation exponent λ=d_f, and density decay exponent α=1-d_s/2 are obtained.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to characterize the non-equilibrium dynamics and ageing phenomena of the voter model on fractal substrates, where geometry (d_f) and diffusive transport (d_s) are decoupled, extending exact correlator envelope results beyond regular lattices.
AI.method: Fractal substrate with nearest-neighbour interactions is modelled via a space-dependent diffusion constant D(r)~r^{-θ}, with spectral index θ a function of d_f and d_s. A scaling ansatz is applied to the equations of motion of the correlators to derive the dynamic scaling functions.
AI.result: Generic ageing phenomenology is confirmed. The dynamic exponent z=2+θ and autocorrelation exponent λ=d_f are derived. The dynamic scaling functions depend only on the spectral dimension d_s. The envelope of the active-interface density decays with exponent α=1-d_s/2 for d_s<2, confirming prior numerical simulations.
AI.conclusion: The voter model on fractal substrates exhibits ageing governed by the spectral dimension, with exact envelope exponents and scaling functions depending solely on d_s, validating earlier numerical findings for the interface density decay.

title: Carrier duality from the convergence of Dirac fermions and high-order van Hove singularities
summary: The convergence of highly mobile Dirac fermions and flat-band heavy electrons offers a paradigm for emergent quantum phenomena. However, experimental realization of such intriguing state remains elusive. In this study, we report a dual carrier regime in the kagome metal Co3In2S2, wherein the charge transport is governed by high-mobility electrons while the thermodynamic responses exhibit heavy-electron behavior. This exotic duality arises from the coexistence of topological Dirac fermions and flat-band high-order (4th-order) Van Hove singularities (HOVHSs) at the Fermi surface, as revealed by magnetic-torque quantum oscillation and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. The interaction between Dirac and HOVHS-derived carriers can be captured by a minimal two-pocket model, manifesting as sublinear resistivity above ~100 K and field-induced non-Fermi-liquid behavior at low temperatures. Our study establishes Co3In2S2 as a model platform for exploring many-body physics at the intersection of topology and correlation effects, and provides a foundational framework for designing quantum materials hosting diverse emergent states.

AI.tldr: Co3In2S2 kagome metal exhibits a dual-carrier regime where high-mobility Dirac electrons coexist with flat-band heavy electrons, stemming from Dirac fermions and 4th-order Van Hove singularities at the Fermi surface.
AI.motivation: The interplay of highly mobile Dirac fermions and flat-band heavy electrons is predicted to host emergent quantum phenomena, but such states remain experimentally unrealized. This work aims to realize and characterize such a coexistence in a real material.
AI.method: Magnetic-torque quantum oscillation and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) were used to resolve the electronic structure. Transport (resistivity) and thermodynamic measurements probed the dual carrier behavior, interpreted via a minimal two-pocket model.
AI.result: Charge transport is dominated by high-mobility electrons, while thermodynamic responses show heavy-electron behavior. The duality is attributed to coexisting topological Dirac fermions and flat-band 4th-order Van Hove singularities (HOVHSs) at the Fermi surface. Signatures include sublinear resistivity above ~100 K and field-induced non-Fermi-liquid behavior at low temperatures.
AI.conclusion: Co3In2S2 is established as a model platform for many-body physics at the intersection of topology and correlation, providing a framework for designing quantum materials with diverse emergent states.

title: Compressive Splitting in Brittle Solids: The Inverse of Wrinkling in Sheets
comment: To appear in Physical Review Letters
summary: Axial splitting is the dominant failure mode of brittle solids under compression, yet its mechanical origin remains unclear. We show that clamped loading platens suppress lateral Poisson expansion, generating boundary-induced tensile stresses at the specimen interior -- the compressive analog of wrinkling in stretched sheets. This mechanism provides a predictive strength law, relating axial splitting to tensile strength, geometry, and confinement pressure. This is validated against diverse materials ranging from rocks to ceramics, establishing axial splitting as a geometry-controlled elastic process rather than a stochastic flaw problem.

AI.tldr: Axial splitting in brittle solids under compression arises from boundary-induced tensile stresses caused by clamped platens suppressing Poisson expansion, yielding a predictive strength law validated across rocks and ceramics.
AI.motivation: Axial splitting is the dominant failure mode of brittle solids under compression, yet its mechanical origin remains unclear.
AI.method: Clamped loading platens suppress lateral Poisson expansion, generating boundary-induced tensile stresses at the specimen interior, analogous to wrinkling in stretched sheets. This mechanism yields a predictive strength law relating axial splitting to tensile strength, geometry, and confinement pressure.
AI.result: The predicted strength law is validated against diverse materials ranging from rocks to ceramics.
AI.conclusion: Axial splitting is established as a geometry-controlled elastic process rather than a stochastic flaw problem.

title: Benchmarking higher-ranking multipoles and polarizability tensors for small molecular systems
summary:
Molecular properties govern how molecules interact with one another or external fields. Accurate molecular properties are essential for constructing intermolecular interaction models, and to achieve high accuracy we need to go beyond leading-order (dipolar) terms.
  This work presents CCSD(T) references for 73 small non-spin-polarized molecules for molecular dipole and quadrupole moments, and dipole-dipole and quadrupole-quadrupole polarizabilities. Using these results, we provide a holistic performance analysis of molecular properties computed with HF, MP2, CCSD, and a wide range of density-functional methods. Additionally, we investigate in detail what levels of basis sets are required to simultaneously describe all properties in the data set.
  The best-performing density functionals for all four properties are the asymptotically cor- rected hybrid GGAs B97-3-AC, closely followed by PBE0-AC. Surprisingly, modern meta- GGAs and range-separated functionals perform inconsistently, with large errors in the quadrupo- lar properties. These results have direct implications for methods for intermolecular interac- tions, such as symmetry-adapted perturbation theory based on density functional theory, or for the quality of properties and interactions in machine-learning datasets.
  Finally, for DFT methods, the Jensen aug-pcseg-2 basis set is a computationally efficient alternative to more established basis sets, but for generating correlated references, third-row elements benefit from core polarization, and double augmentation is strictly necessary for quadrupole-quadrupole polarizabilities.

AI.tldr: CCSD(T) references for dipole/quadrupole moments and dipole-dipole/quadrupole-quadrupole polarizabilities of 73 small molecules are presented, benchmarking HF, MP2, CCSD, and many DFT methods plus basis-set requirements.
AI.motivation: Accurate molecular properties are essential for building intermolecular interaction models, and high accuracy requires going beyond leading-order (dipolar) terms to include quadrupolar and higher-order contributions.
AI.method: CCSD(T) reference calculations for 73 small non-spin-polarized molecules covering molecular dipole and quadrupole moments, dipole-dipole and quadrupole-quadrupole polarizabilities; holistic performance analysis of HF, MP2, CCSD, and a wide range of density-functional methods; systematic investigation of the basis-set levels needed to describe all properties simultaneously.
AI.result: The asymptotically corrected hybrid GGAs B97-3-AC and PBE0-AC perform best across all four properties. Modern meta-GGAs and range-separated functionals are inconsistent, showing large errors in quadrupolar properties. The Jensen aug-pcseg-2 basis set is a computationally efficient alternative for DFT, while correlated references for third-row elements benefit from core polarization and double augmentation is strictly necessary for quadrupole-quadrupole polarizabilities.
AI.conclusion: The findings directly inform methods for intermolecular interactions, such as DFT-based symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT), and the quality of properties and interactions in machine-learning datasets.

title: Scalable Multiple Electron Transport Architectures for Feedback Traceable Current Sources
summary:
We present a scalable electron-counting current cell based on a floating gate architecture operated as a Multiple Electron Transport device (MET). The system enables controlled injection, transport, and precise quantification of discrete charge packets using the sensor non-destructive multiple readout capability. We repurposed the charge-injection technique, jointly with the electron-resolution capability, for a controlled generation of quantized charge packets for an electron-traceable current source.
  Scalable architectures based on parallel and series multi-amplifier configurations are explored. Experimental results confirm noise reduction following the square root of the number of independent measurements and demonstrate stable, programmable output current. This approach provides a compact and scalable platform for electron-counting current sources and precision quantum metrology applications.

AI.tldr: A scalable electron-counting current cell is proposed using a floating-gate Multiple Electron Transport (MET) device, achieving controlled injection, transport, and quantification of discrete charge packets for an electron-traceable current source.
AI.motivation: The work aims to realize a compact, scalable, and precise platform for electron-counting current sources and quantum metrology, leveraging controlled quantized charge packet generation for traceable current.
AI.method: The authors repurpose a charge-injection technique combined with electron-resolution capability in a floating-gate MET architecture. Non-destructive multiple readout enables quantification of discrete charge packets, and scalable parallel and series multi-amplifier configurations are explored.
AI.result: Experimental results confirm noise reduction proportional to the square root of the number of independent measurements and demonstrate stable, programmable output current.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach offers a compact and scalable platform for electron-counting current sources and precision quantum metrology applications.

title: Heterogeneous planar diffusion with axisymmetric power-law decaying diffusion coefficient under stochastic resetting
summary: We analyse two-dimensional isotropic heterogeneous diffusion with a radially decaying diffusion coefficient $D(ρ)=D_0/ρ^2$, subject to Poissonian stochastic resetting to the origin. Since multiplicative noise makes the process interpretation-dependent, we treat the Itô, Stratonovich, and Hänggi--Klimontovich prescriptions within a single approach. For each, we obtain the exact probability density function, the non-equilibrium stationary state induced by resetting, the mean squared displacement, and the first-passage properties. The non-equilibrium stationary state is governed by modified Bessel functions and departs from the Laplace form found for homogeneous diffusion under resetting, while the mean squared displacement saturates at long times as $\langleρ^2\rangle\sim\bar{r}^{-1/2}$, $\bar{r}$ being the resetting rate. The mean first-passage time to an absorbing boundary exhibits an optimal resetting rate at which it is minimised. In addition, we incorporate memory effects through a subordination (continuous-time random walk) approach with a power-law kernel, deriving the fractional Fokker--Planck equation together with the non-equilibrium stationary state, the mean squared displacement expressed via the three-parameter Mittag-Leffler function, and the first-passage statistics; the optimal resetting rate increases as the memory exponent decreases.

AI.tldr: Exact solution of 2D heterogeneous diffusion with D(ρ)=D0/ρ² under Poissonian resetting, treated consistently under Itô, Stratonovich, and Hänggi–Klimontovich interpretations, plus an extension to memory effects via subordination.
AI.motivation: Heterogeneous diffusion with a radially decaying diffusion coefficient and stochastic resetting are both well-studied separately, but their combination is not. Since multiplicative noise renders the process interpretation-dependent, a unified treatment of the three stochastic prescriptions is needed to disentangle interpretation artifacts from genuine resetting-induced physics.
AI.method: Analytical study of 2D isotropic heterogeneous diffusion with D(ρ)=D0/ρ² under Poissonian resetting to the origin, using a single framework that covers the Itô, Stratonovich, and Hänggi–Klimontovich prescriptions. Memory effects are incorporated through subordination (continuous-time random walk) with a power-law waiting-time kernel, yielding a fractional Fokker–Planck equation.
AI.result: For each prescription: exact probability density function, non-equilibrium stationary state, mean squared displacement, and first-passage properties. The stationary state involves modified Bessel functions and differs from the Laplace form of homogeneous diffusion under resetting. The MSD saturates at long times as ⟨ρ²⟩ ~ r̄^(−1/2), with r̄ the resetting rate, and the mean first-passage time to an absorbing boundary is minimised at an optimal resetting rate. Under subordination, the MSD is expressed via the three-parameter Mittag-Leffler function, and the optimal resetting rate increases as the memory exponent decreases.
AI.conclusion: Resetting generically produces a Bessel-type non-equilibrium stationary state and a saturating MSD in this heterogeneous geometry, with an optimal resetting rate that can be tuned by memory. The results are prescription-dependent in detail but structurally analogous across Itô, Stratonovich, and Hänggi–Klimontovich interpretations.

title: Slave-Rotor and Auxiliary Chain Analysis of the Mott Transition in a Modified Periodic Anderson Model
summary: The Mott-Hubbard transition is a paradigmatic phenomenon driven by strong electronic correlations. We investigate this transition in a three-orbital modified periodic Anderson model using slave-rotor mean-field theory. A minimal two-site cluster extension is introduced to understand the minimal effects of short-range spatial correlations. In comparison to the single-site solution, short-range spatial correlations reveal a shift of the transition point. Going beyond the slave-rotor analysis, we also evaluate the dynamical self-energy and map it onto the boundary Green's function of a non-interacting semi-infinite auxiliary chain. For the metallic phase, the resulting hopping pattern corresponds to a topologically trivial generalized Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain. This construction provides a framework for exploring the possible topological character of the Mott transition in this model.

AI.tldr: This work studies the Mott-Hubbard transition in a three-orbital modified periodic Anderson model using slave-rotor mean-field theory, and introduces a minimal two-site cluster to capture short-range spatial correlations. It further maps the dynamical self-energy onto the boundary Green's function of a non-interacting semi-infinite auxiliary chain, revealing a topologically trivial generalized Su-Schrieffer-Heeger character in the metallic phase.
AI.motivation: The Mott-Hubbard transition is a paradigmatic strong-correlation phenomenon, and understanding how short-range spatial correlations affect the transition point, as well as exploring possible topological character of the transition, motivates this investigation.
AI.method: Slave-rotor mean-field theory applied to a three-orbital modified periodic Anderson model; a minimal two-site cluster extension to include short-range spatial correlations; evaluation of the dynamical self-energy and its mapping onto the boundary Green's function of a non-interacting semi-infinite auxiliary chain.
AI.result: Compared with the single-site solution, short-range spatial correlations produce a shift of the transition point. In the metallic phase, the resulting hopping pattern corresponds to a topologically trivial generalized Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain.
AI.conclusion: The auxiliary-chain mapping provides a framework for exploring the possible topological character of the Mott transition in this model.

title: Experimentally validated process-microstructure-property relations of bainitic steels derived from phase-field simulations
summary: This study examines the impact of processing conditions, such as thermalprocessing, on the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties. Spe-cial emphasis is placed on microstructural features obtained from three-dimensional phase-field simulations, which provide detailed insights into bai-nite morphology, phase distribution and retained austenite content. Thesesimulated microstructures are correlated with changes in yield strength undermultiaxial load, as represented in the yield surface of the material. The re-sults demonstrate that optimized processing routes can refine the microstruc-ture, enhance mechanical properties and significantly alter the yield surfacecharacteristics. These findings provide valuable insights for the design andapplication of bainitic steels, as well as for the development of predictivemodels linking process-structure-property relationships.

AI.tldr: This study uses 3D phase-field simulations to link thermal processing conditions to bainitic steel microstructure and multiaxial yield behavior, showing that optimized processing refines microstructure, improves mechanical properties, and reshapes the yield surface.
AI.motivation: Understanding how processing conditions govern microstructure and mechanical response is essential for tailoring bainitic steels, yet the connection between simulated microstructural features and multiaxial yield behavior remains insufficiently explored.
AI.method: The impact of processing conditions, particularly thermal processing, is examined. Microstructural features are obtained from three-dimensional phase-field simulations, capturing bainite morphology, phase distribution, and retained austenite content. These simulated microstructures are then correlated with changes in yield strength under multiaxial loading, expressed through the material's yield surface.
AI.result: Optimized processing routes refine the microstructure, enhance mechanical properties, and significantly alter yield surface characteristics.
AI.conclusion: The findings offer valuable guidance for the design and application of bainitic steels and support the development of predictive models describing process-structure-property relationships.

title: The Superconducting Talbot Effect in Phased-Array Josephson Junctions
summary: We introduce the superconducting Talbot effect---a macroscopic quantum self-imaging phenomenon occurring when proximitized Cooper pairs propagate through a ballistic two-dimensional electron gas. By configuring periodic superconducting leads into a phased-array Josephson junction with programmable phase differences, we demonstrate active steering of the resulting superconducting Talbot carpet. To overcome transport resolution limits, we design a Vernier-scale collector array that performs sub-wavelength sampling of the fractional Talbot pattern. This approach maps real-space quantum interference with high robustness to disorder, enabling direct extraction of Fermi wavelengths across helical, spin-degenerate, and spin-orbit-split Fermi surfaces. Tight-binding numerical calculations on a square lattice validate the real-space interference patterns. Our results establish a versatile framework for coherent wavefront engineering and quantum materials diagnostics in superconducting optics.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the superconducting Talbot effect, a macroscopic quantum self-imaging phenomenon where proximitized Cooper pairs propagate through a ballistic 2D electron gas. Using a phased-array Josephson junction and a Vernier-scale collector array for sub-wavelength sampling, the authors actively steer the Talbot carpet and extract Fermi wavelengths across different Fermi surface types, validating results with tight-binding calculations.
AI.motivation: Conventional Talbot self-imaging has been explored in optics, but its superconducting analogue involving coherent Cooper pair propagation through a ballistic 2D electron gas remains unexplored. Achieving active control and high-resolution readout of such quantum interference patterns is challenging due to transport resolution limits and disorder sensitivity.
AI.method: Periodic superconducting leads are configured into a phased-array Josephson junction with programmable phase differences to actively steer the superconducting Talbot carpet arising from proximitized Cooper pairs. A Vernier-scale collector array is designed to perform sub-wavelength sampling of the fractional Talbot pattern. Tight-binding numerical calculations on a square lattice validate the real-space interference patterns.
AI.result: The Vernier-scale collector array enables sub-wavelength sampling that maps real-space quantum interference with high robustness to disorder. This allows direct extraction of Fermi wavelengths across helical, spin-degenerate, and spin-orbit-split Fermi surfaces. Tight-binding calculations on a square lattice confirm the observed real-space interference patterns.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a versatile framework for coherent wavefront engineering and quantum materials diagnostics in superconducting optics, with the superconducting Talbot effect serving as a robust platform for probing quantum interference and Fermi surface properties.

title: Non-equilibrium dynamics of drift-diffusion process under threshold resetting
summary: We study the emergence of non-equilibrium steady states (NESS) in stochastic processes under threshold resetting, an event-driven protocol in which the system resets to its initial configuration upon crossing a prescribed spatial boundary (threshold). In contrast to externally driven resetting, whose steady-state properties are well understood, the behavior under threshold resetting remains largely unexplored. We derive general conditions for the existence of a NESS and show that, whenever it exists, the steady state at a given position $x$ can be expressed as the ratio of two fundamental quantities: the mean local time (MLT) at $x$ and the mean first-passage time (MFPT) to hit the threshold. In particular, for noisy systems, a finite MFPT guarantees the existence of a NESS. As an illustrative example, we analyze a drift-diffusion process in one dimension and uncover rich intermediate-time dynamics, including anomalous relaxation in the spatial distribution, damped oscillations in the moments and in the mean-squared displacement (MSD), governed by system parameters. Our findings provide a general understanding of the emergence of non-equilibrium steady states and relaxation dynamics under threshold resetting, revealing how induced events shape the spatial and temporal properties of a broad class of stochastic processes.

AI.tldr: Stochastic processes under threshold resetting (resetting to initial configuration upon crossing a spatial boundary) can develop a non-equilibrium steady state (NESS), given by the ratio of the mean local time at x to the mean first-passage time to the threshold. A one-dimensional drift-diffusion example exhibits anomalous spatial relaxation and damped oscillations in moments and MSD.
AI.motivation: Externally driven resetting is well understood in terms of its steady-state properties, but the behavior of systems under threshold resetting—an event-driven protocol where reset occurs upon crossing a prescribed spatial boundary—remains largely unexplored. The authors aim to characterize when a NESS emerges in this setting and how induced reset events shape spatial and temporal relaxation dynamics.
AI.method: The authors analyze stochastic processes subject to threshold resetting and derive general conditions for the existence of a NESS. They express the steady-state probability at position x as the ratio of the mean local time (MLT) at x to the mean first-passage time (MFPT) to the threshold. They illustrate the framework with a one-dimensional drift-diffusion process, examining intermediate-time dynamics.
AI.result: A general condition for NESS existence is obtained: whenever the steady state exists, it equals the ratio of MLT at x to the MFPT to the threshold. For noisy systems, a finite MFPT guarantees NESS existence. In the drift-diffusion example, rich intermediate-time dynamics appear, including anomalous relaxation of the spatial distribution and damped oscillations in the moments and mean-squared displacement (MSD), controlled by system parameters.
AI.conclusion: Threshold resetting yields a general understanding of NESS emergence and relaxation dynamics, showing how induced reset events shape the spatial and temporal properties of a broad class of stochastic processes.

title: Spin-Orbit Induced Confinement of Correlated Bound States in the Continuum
summary: Repulsively bound doublons are two-particle composites formed by strong interactions and are usually separated from the scattering continuum. Introducing spin-orbit coupling fundamentally alters the underlying band structure, providing a powerful tuning knob to shift these isolated pairs toward this continuum. However, because entering such a regime typically dictates immediate dissociation, whether this coupling can drive these pairs inside while preserving their bound nature constitutes a fundamental unresolved challenge. Here we show that spin-orbit coupling in the one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model can drive doublons into the two-particle scattering continuum. Most of these states hybridize with extended channels and decay, whereas a subset remains decoupled and spatially bound, forming many-body bound states in the continuum (BICs). We map the interacting two-particle problem onto a two-dimensional lattice of coupled acoustic cavities, and experimentally observe both the radiating doublon continuum and the confined BIC states. These results demonstrate that spin-orbit coupling can turn selected doublons into interaction-induced BICs, deepening the understanding of continuum physics for interaction-bound pairs.

AI.tldr: Spin-orbit coupling in the 1D Fermi-Hubbard model can drive repulsively bound doublons into the two-particle scattering continuum; most hybridize and decay, but a subset survives as spatially bound many-body states in the continuum (BICs), experimentally realized via a mapped 2D lattice of coupled acoustic cavities.
AI.motivation: Repulsively bound doublons are normally isolated from the scattering continuum by strong interactions. Spin-orbit coupling reshapes the band structure and offers a tuning knob to push these pairs toward the continuum, but entering that regime usually causes immediate dissociation. Whether such coupling can move doublons into the continuum while preserving their bound nature was an unresolved fundamental question.
AI.method: The authors study spin-orbit coupling in the one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model for the interacting two-particle problem. They map this problem onto a two-dimensional lattice of coupled acoustic cavities and experimentally observe both the radiating doublon continuum and the confined BIC states.
AI.result: Spin-orbit coupling drives doublons into the two-particle scattering continuum. Most of these states hybridize with extended channels and decay, whereas a subset remains decoupled and spatially bound, forming many-body bound states in the continuum (BICs). Both the radiating doublon continuum and the confined BIC states were experimentally observed.
AI.conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling can turn selected doublons into interaction-induced BICs, deepening the understanding of continuum physics for interaction-bound pairs.

title: Highly Lattice-Mismatched Selective Area Epitaxy and Coalescence of PbSe Nanostructures on GaAs
summary: Selective area growth of PbSe has the potential to realize deterministic placement of high-density, defect-tolerant nanostructure networks toward a scalable quantum platform. PbSe is a narrow bandgap semiconductor with advantageous (opto)electronic properties that has been shown to have a desirable defect-tolerance, enabling bright emission even when grown on highly-dissimilar platforms, and could be leveraged in combination with selective growth for site-selective quantum emitters and low-disorder hybrid nanowire networks. In this work, we achieve site-selective growth of well-faceted and ordered PbSe nanostructures, despite a large 8% lattice mismatch. Structural and morphological characterization reveal that $>$99% of selectively grown islands within 100 nm opening are single-orientation and cube-on-cube oriented with sub-nm root-mean-square surface roughness. Defect analysis showed that 74% of the islands and 86% of the coalesced regions between different mask openings were free of threading dislocations. These PbSe islands achieved equivalent emission in the mid-infrared despite having a higher surface-to-volume ratio than the planar control. Further, we present a gate-tunable two-terminal Josephson junction fabricated from the PbSe nanowires grown with conditions identified in this study. The combination of the accessible selective growth regime, morphological control of island growth and demonstrations of optical and electrical transport properties indicates promise for PbSe SAG as a defect-tolerant scalable quantum platform.
